articles.title: Asus routers escape US router ban, but TP-Link is still waiting
articles.text:
What just happened? Good news for fans of Asus routers: the FCC has announced that the Defense Department does not believe they pose a security risk. That means the devices have been granted "conditional approval" and are exempt from the foreign-made-router ban. The Taiwanese firm will be happy with the outcome, but things aren't looking rosy for rival TP-Link.
Asus' exemption lasts until March 6, 2028 – approximately 18 months from when it was issued. It covers the company's RT Series, ROG GT Series, ROG Strix GS Series, TUF Gaming Series, ExpertWiFi Series, ZenWiFi Mesh Series, 5G MiFi Series, wireless repeaters, and wireless access points.
The FCC added foreign-produced consumer routers to its Covered List in March, blocking authorization of new models without conditional approval from the Department of War or Homeland Security.
The agency said foreign-produced routers create supply-chain vulnerabilities and severe cybersecurity risks, and pointed to their role in the Volt, Flax, and Salt Typhoon campaigns as justification for adding them to the Covered List.
In April, Netgear became the first router brand to avoid the ban. Amazon-owned Eero/Leo, Nokia, SpaceX/Starlink, and Askey are among the other companies granted exemptions.
Part of the application process requires manufacturers to offer a plan for establishing or expanding manufacturing in the United States for their routers.
Asus recently revealed its new generation of Wi-Fi 8 routers, including the ROG Rapture GT-BN98 series and ZenWiFi BN12 mesh system. The former is already available in Canada, with a wider rollout starting in October. Asus says US launch details will follow, making the exemption particularly well timed.
TP-Link, meanwhile, still hasn't received an exemption. The company met with FCC officials in April to argue that TP-Link Systems is an American business headquartered in Irvine, California. But that argument has yet to secure it a place alongside its rivals on the approval list.
The uncertainty is casting a dark cloud over TP-Link's own Wi-Fi 8 plans. Its Archer 8 announcement targeted an October 8 release, but launching new models in the US still depends on getting the regulatory green light.
For anyone already using a TP-Link router, there's no need to start shopping for a replacement because of this ban. It affects authorization of new models; previously authorized routers can still be sold and used.

articles.title: Rocket Report: Europe joins the commercial launch club; a Ravn X sighting?
articles.text:
Welcome to Edition 9.10 of the Rocket Report! This week we’re celebrating a historic moment in Europe when a German rocket company successfully put its launch vehicle into orbit. Isar Aerospace became the first purely commercial European company to reach orbit, and impressively it did so on just its second launch attempt. How quickly can they scale up operations? How quickly will the second European launch firm reach this goal? Big questions, which for now we don’t have answers to.
As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don’t want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.
Isar Aerospace takes a huge step forward. Isar Aerospace, founded in 2018 by three students at a German university, successfully launched a privately developed rocket into low-Earth orbit on Saturday from a Norwegian spaceport inside the Arctic Circle. The two-stage rocket, Spectrum, became the first fully commercial launch vehicle in Europe to reach orbit, Ars reports. With Saturday’s success, Isar becomes the clear leader among a pack of several European launch startups vying to inject some competition into Europe’s stagnant launch market.
Private capital emerges … It took eight years for Isar to get to orbit, a timetable similar to other successful commercial rocket startups in the West. In that time, the company raised roughly $1 billion through several private financing rounds and now has a workforce of nearly 500 employees. European space officials hope a jolt of competition will light a fire under the continent’s rocket industry. European governments are accustomed to footing the bill and having a say in where rockets are built, a procurement model known as geographical return, or geo-return. The paradigm is different with companies like Isar, which established themselves on a privately funded basis, with ambitions to eventually attract commercial and government business.
Long-forgotten space plane is back? Ars Technica has written precisely one article about Ravn X, an autonomous aircraft and launch vehicle under development by Aevum. This was back in December 2020. We haven’t covered it since, I think it’s safe to say, there is a fair amount of skepticism about whether the project to build the space plane was all that realistic. And time has largely proved us right. The company’s initial target of an orbital mission in 2021 came and went. We largely forgot about the vehicle. Then something mysterious showed up at Long Beach Airport.
Don’t get too excited … TWZ reports that a handful of aviation photographers got a surprise eyeful of a very sleek and large aircraft silhouette last week at the airport and later learned that it was likely a mockup of Ravn X. Later on, in posts on X, Aevum founder Jay Skylus said the company “conducted Test 2 of Ravn X SN0 early this morning. Ravn X completed its first fully autonomous taxi. ~37 minutes of autonomy. We’re reviewing the telemetry and test data now and will share more as soon as I can.” We are not expecting any flights imminently. (submitted by Onychomys)
The Ars Technica Rocket Report
The easiest way to keep up with Eric Berger’s and Stephen Clark’s reporting on all things space is to sign up for our newsletter. We’ll collect their stories and deliver them straight to your inbox.
UK invests big time in northern spaceport. This week, the United Kingdom unveiled a new national space strategy that seeks to “drive growth, strengthen security and back everyday technologies.” As part of efforts to reindustrialize the country, the government is investing 7.8 billion pounds ($10.5 billion) through 2030. About 40 percent of the funding will go toward strengthening connectivity, including the Connectivity in Low Earth Orbit and SKYNET defense communications programs, which “play a pivotal role in keeping our Armed Forces connected wherever they are in the world.”
German rockets to launch from there … The UK government also wants to help push forward a spaceport under development in Shetland, an archipelago north of the Scottish mainland. The government will provide 30 million pounds ($40.5 million) for the SaxaVord Spaceport in Shetland, with the aim of “helping Britain and our partners to launch satellites without relying on countries further afield while creating new jobs.” No orbital rocket has ever successfully launched from the United Kingdom. The main tenant of SaxaVord is German launch company Rocket Factory Augsburg. (submitted by iCowboy)
Firefly to launch from Sweden. Firefly Aerospace announced on Wednesday a multi-launch agreement with SSC Space for two Alpha rocket launches from Sweden’s Esrange Space Center. Targeted to launch no earlier than 2028, the missions will serve Sweden’s national security customers as well as additional commercial rideshare customers.
More to come … Jason Kim, CEO of Firefly Aerospace, said more Alpha launches will follow. “These first two missions are just the start of a long-term, multi-launch partnership with SSC Space that will provide assured access to space for years to come,” he said. SSC Space secured the full payload capacity and can allocate payload space to its government and commercial customers, providing flexible accommodations and launch opportunities for the European satellite market.
Avio seeks higher flight rate. Avio is looking to boost the pace of Vega-C rocket flights to six missions per year, roughly double the current level, and potentially go another 50 percent higher, Aviation Week reports. “We are working to increase, as a first step, the cadence of Vega to six per year, and potentially a second step to nine per year,” Giulio Ranzo said Wednesday during the International Space Summit in Paris.
Solid production is not so solid … The Vega-C rocket is used heavily by institutions for launch in Europe, where demand is rising. “We will follow what they need, what they ask us, and we will try to adapt to continue providing the service,” Ranzo said. One of the challenges in ramping up is that the Vega-C used the same solid rocket motors employed on Ariane 6, which is also looking to boost output. The combination is creating supply-chain bottlenecks that industry and government are trying to address.
Stoke Space eyes larger rocket. Stoke Space announced Tuesday that it has raised another significant round of funding, $1 billion, as it makes a final push toward its debut launch next year. The Washington-based launch company also revealed plans for a larger medium-lift vehicle, Ars reports. The quantity of new funding will enable the company to accelerate work on a larger “Block 2” version of the Nova rocket, capable of lifting 15 metric tons to low-Earth orbit in a fully reusable configuration.
Block 2 will rock you … “We have already started development on a larger vehicle, and we felt like now is the time to pour gas on that fire and really start full-force development of the larger vehicle, and so that’s the reason for the timing,” Stoke co-founder and Chief Executive Andy Lapsa said. The Nova Pathfinder vehicle has a diameter of about 12.5 feet, slightly larger than SpaceX’s Falcon 9 vehicle, although it is considerably shorter. The Block 2 version of Nova is intended to have a 15-foot diameter, Lapsa said. Stoke is targeting 2029 for the debut launch of Block 2.
Ariane 64 gets with Amazon for some more. Arianespace and Amazon Leo announced Wednesday an agreement at the International Space Summit in Paris for six additional Ariane 64 launches to continue deploying the Amazon Leo constellation into low-Earth orbit. The new order brings the total number of Amazon Leo launches with Arianespace to 24, up from 18, with missions scheduled through 2031 from Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana.
Arianespace, the on-time provider? … To the surprise of some observers, including your humble correspondent, Arianespace has proven to be a more reliable launch partner to Amazon than the other two providers who inked deals with Amazon in 2022, United Launch Alliance and Blue Origin. But Ariane 6 has gotten through its teething pains without major issues, unlike Vulcan and New Glenn. “We committed early because we believed in what Arianespace was building, and they’ve executed mission after mission,” said Chris Weber, vice president of Amazon Leo business and product. “Expanding from 18 to 24 launches reflects our confidence in Ariane 6 and our continued investment in European launch capability.”
Nyx will fly on Ariane 6. Arianespace and The Exploration Company announced this week that Nyx, the reusable space capsule developed by The Exploration Company, will launch into orbit on an Ariane 6 rocket from French Guiana. The Exploration Company chief executive, Hélène Huby, has said she is targeting late 2028 for the launch of this spacecraft, which is due to fly a cargo mission to the International Space Station.
Commercial cargo redux … The launch deal follows the award of a service contract to The Exploration Company by the European Space Agency worth 760 million euros ($880 million) to support the development of Nyx, a demonstration mission, and two operational cargo missions. “We started the development of Nyx with private funding only, and we are now at a technical maturity level where ESA and Member States’ public funding can support us massively, as anchor clients, to help us finalize the vehicle,” Huby said.
Does Europe need a massive rocket? Speaking of Huby and The Exploration Company, the company also announced a $450 million Series C funding round this week, Ars reports. As part of this, the company will continue development of the Storm rocket engine, which is projected to have a thrust of about 400,000 pound-feet. This would be used to power a reusable rocket intended to launch 40 metric tons in reusable mode and 60 tons in expendable mode.
How to stay relevant … The expendable Ariane 6 rocket, by contrast, has a maximum lift capacity of about 20 tons. “If Europe wants to stay relevant—we will not be relevant without a massive rocket at a massive cadence,” Huby said during a teleconference with reporters on Tuesday. “And to do that we need a massive engine, and right now this is something we just do not have in Europe.” An aggressive timeline for the rocket’s development, she said, is 2033.
Terran R gets on-ramped by NASA. NASA said this week it has awarded a “Launch Services II” contract to Relativity Space that allows for on-ramping the Terran R rocket into the agency’s launch services program. Accordingly, the Terran R launch service will be available to NASA for future missions, including science, research, and human spaceflight.
Don’t expect Terran R to win awards right away … NASA still wants to see a new rocket like Terran R, which has yet to make its debut, demonstrate success in flight. However, by receiving this contract, Relativity can now follow a pathway for new launch service providers to compete for future missions. The current ordering period covers missions through December 2032.
Next three launches
September 13: Falcon 9 | O3b mPOWER 11, 12, 13 | Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Fla. | 18:49 UTC
September 15: Vega C | Sentinel-3C, Flex | Guiana Space Center, French Guiana | 01:21 UTC
September 15: Zhuque-2E | Unknown Payload | Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, China | 06:25 UTC
Eric Berger is the senior space editor at Ars Technica, covering everything from astronomy to private space to NASA policy, and author of two books: Liftoff, about the rise of SpaceX; and Reentry, on the development of the Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon. A certified meteorologist, Eric lives in Houston.

articles.title: Oracle vai gastar mais R$ 3,7 bilhões com cortes de funcionários
articles.text:
A Oracle vai gastar mais US$ 700 milhões (cerca de R$ 3,7 bilhões) com seu plano de reestruturação, que inclui cortes de funcionários, rescisão de contratos e outras despesas relacionadas à redução de custos. Com o novo valor, o custo total previsto para o programa no ano fiscal de 2026 chega a aproximadamente US$ 2,8 bilhões (cerca de R$ 14,8 bilhões).
A informação foi divulgada pela empresa em documento regulatório nesta sexta-feira (11). Segundo a Oracle, parte das despesas está relacionada à adoção de inteligência artificial (IA) em algumas funções da companhia. No ano fiscal anterior, a empresa havia destinado cerca de US$ 2,1 bilhões (cerca de R$ 11,1 bilhões) à reestruturação.
O movimento acontece enquanto a Oracle tenta reduzir custos em algumas áreas, ao mesmo tempo em que direciona bilhões de dólares para ampliar sua infraestrutura de computação em nuvem e atender à crescente demanda por serviços de IA.
IA aumenta demanda por infraestrutura
A pressão para investir em infraestrutura de IA aumentou depois de a Oracle registrar mais de US$ 30 bilhões (cerca de R$ 159 bilhões) em novos contratos de computação em nuvem relacionados à tecnologia no primeiro trimestre fiscal.
Com isso, a carteira de contratos da empresa chegou a US$ 664 bilhões (cerca de R$ 3,5 trilhões). A Oracle informou que aproximadamente metade desse valor deve se transformar em vendas nos próximos 36 meses.
Apesar do tamanho dos novos contratos, a companhia afirma que a maior parte deles não exigirá grandes desembolsos adicionais de capital. Isso ocorre porque parte dos acordos envolve pagamentos antecipados de clientes ou o fornecimento dos próprios equipamentos necessários para a operação.
A estratégia é importante para uma empresa que vem ampliando fortemente os gastos com data centers e outros recursos necessários para sustentar seus serviços de IA.
Leia mais:
- Oracle supera expectativas com boom da IA e vê ações subirem 7% após balanço
- Big Techs acumulam R$ 5,6 trilhões em contratos para a corrida da IA
- Oracle acerta contrato com Pentágono; valor pode chegar a R$ 35,7 bi
Caixa ainda preocupa
- A expansão também aumentou a preocupação dos investidores com o caixa da Oracle. No primeiro trimestre fiscal, a companhia registrou fluxo de caixa livre negativo de US$ 5,4 bilhões (cerca de R$ 28,6 bilhões). Apesar de elevado, o valor ficou abaixo da expectativa média dos analistas, que era de um consumo de caixa de US$ 9,56 bilhões (R$ 48,95 bilhões);
- A Oracle também informou que pretende levantar US$ 40 bilhões (cerca de R$ 212 bilhões) em dívida e ações durante o atual ano fiscal para financiar sua expansão. Desse total, US$ 20 bilhões (R$ 102,4 bilhões) já haviam sido obtidos por meio de uma venda de ações no primeiro trimestre;
- Os resultados financeiros ajudaram a mostrar o tamanho da transformação pela qual a empresa passa. A receita do primeiro trimestre fiscal cresceu 30%, para US$ 19,3 bilhões (cerca de R$ 102,3 bilhões), enquanto a companhia também registrou resultados acima das expectativas do mercado;
- Ao mesmo tempo, os cortes de funcionários e o aumento dos gastos com infraestrutura mostram os dois lados da estratégia da Oracle: reduzir despesas em determinadas áreas para liberar recursos enquanto acelera os investimentos necessários para disputar o mercado de IA.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Anthropic spent this week in hot water over cybersecurity
articles.text:
After admitting earlier this year that its AI models had hacked other companies’ systems on a handful of occasions, Anthropic released a new report on Wednesday detailing the attacks. It reveals a string of incidents displaying what Anthropic deems its models’ single-minded “recklessness” — and will likely fuel already raging concerns about cybersecurity and AI.
Anthropic spent this week in hot water over cybersecurity
A researcher’s resignation letter went viral, just before the company released details about four models going rogue.
Anthropic spent this week in hot water over cybersecurity
A researcher’s resignation letter went viral, just before the company released details about four models going rogue.
In Anthropic’s report, it detailed four cases this year in which its own AI models hacked an external company or exploited vulnerabilities. In one, an “internal, general-purpose research model” broke into third-party systems, using access tokens and passwords and downloading files. In another, a Claude model attacked a company with a live web application reachable on the public internet and handled user data. A third model accessed a “machine belonging to a third party that it was able to access” — apparently believing it was part of its evaluation exercise, per Anthropic — then used a password it found inside a file to gain admin access to the third party’s internal systems, going on to harvest credentials, modify system settings, and read someone’s personal information. The saga only ended when the model “exhausted its token budget,” per Anthropic.
The most concerning incident involved Claude Mythos 5, Anthropic’s frontier cybersecurity-focused model, which the company said turned out to be the model most likely to perform a “severely harmful” action in testing. The company said Mythos 5 went to “extensive lengths” to upload a “malicious package” to a public repository used by a lot of engineers, and it seemed to try to obfuscate its real goals in its “chain of thought” (a mental scratchpad that AI researchers use to evaluate an AI model’s alignment). In many cases, Anthropic said it appeared that Claude models undertook harmful actions under the assumption they were in a simulation, but researchers also couldn’t confirm that the models truly “believed” that or were just acting like they did.
Anthropic’s incidents, though still concerning, were less coordinated and pervasive than the OpenAI incident that kicked off an industry-wide cybersecurity crisis this summer. That said, there are significant similarities. Anthropic said the most prevalent issues it discovered included a “willingness to take harmful actions in the narrow pursuit of a task,” similar to the “reward-hacking” that preceded the Hugging Face attack. Much like OpenAI, it said its prerelease tests and evaluations failed to catch severe risks.
Anthropic said it had signed an agreement with METR, one of the AI industry’s most prominent third-party AI evaluators, starting with an eight-week research agreement. The agreement grants METR access to transcripts “beyond the window in which the incidents occurred” (likely a subtle dig at OpenAI, which was criticized for limiting access in a deal with METR following the Hugging Face attack). It also said that METR would be able to chat directly with Anthropic employees, “who will be permitted to share confidential information.”
Anthropic’s report came on the heels of the resignation of Jacob Coxon, who had worked on AI pre-training at Anthropic since May and before that spent years working at OpenAI. On Tuesday, he resigned and posted a public letter to X about his reasoning. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” he wrote, adding that neither OpenAI nor Anthropic is “acting responsibly” and rather “racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives.” Coxon added, “Do not underestimate the power of this technology. These will soon be superhuman systems that can hack anything, revolutionize any field overnight, and acquire real power and resources. We have all witnessed the progress in each of these domains, and progress is not slowing.”
Coxon is far from the first AI researcher to raise these types of alarms, nor even the first Anthropic researcher to do so — in February, Anthropic’s Mrinank Sharma resigned and wrote on X, warning that “the world is in peril.”
But Coxon’s post took on additional weight thanks to its timing around the OpenAI and Anthropic hacking revelations. Though the AI industry has seen more than its fair share of hype, the recent cyberattacks by AI agents — enabled by the labs that created them — are real and concerning. Many other researchers at leading AI labs echoed his concerns and issued calls for AI industry employees to sign a public letter from July, which calls for a slowdown in AI development.
”I don’t know how you look at the steady drumbeat of news and events — and that drumbeat is models hacking themselves out of containment, hacking into other companies ,the fact that the companies increasingly can’t control their models … and think this is just hype,” said Michael Kleinman, head of U.S. Policy for the Future of Life Institute.
He added, “The vast majority of Americans, regardless of party — Republican, Independent, Democrat — are looking at the development of AI, the speed with which it’s going, the fact that the companies have no guardrails over what they do, and are saying, ‘Whoa, we do not want this.’”

articles.title: ¿Error de precio? Amazon sigue vendiendo el iPhone 17 a precio de chollo después de que Apple lo suba a 1.109 euros
articles.text:
Ya te avisamos la semana pasada antes de que Apple anunciase los nuevos dispositivos: el iPhone 17 no se iba a renovar y seguía siendo muy buena compra. Hoy la historia cambia un poco: como se esperaba, el iPhone 18 base no se presentó, pero la californiana sorprendió subiendo el precio del iPhone 17 en la Apple Store. Ahora cuesta 1.109 euros y la recomendación ha cambiado un poco, pero Amazon parece que no ha movido el precio que estaba ofreciendo hace días.
El iPhone 17 sigue costando 929 euros en Amazon, que ya es menos de los 959 euros del PVP anterior que fijó Apple en 2025. La oferta ya era buena, pero ahora es grandiosa. La mala noticia es que no va a durar mucho. Es probable que Amazon esté agotando las unidades que ya tenía vendiéndolas a 929 euros y que pronto actualice el precio para vender el dispositivo en una cifra más cercana a los 1.109 euros.
La buena noticia es que, para quien necesite un iPhone nuevo en este momento, el iPhone 17 es una buenísima opción, sobre todo si aprovechas esta oferta a 929 euros. El iPhone 18 no llegará hasta mediados del año que viene, y cuando se presente, muy probablemente lo hará con muy pocas novedades. Su precio se mantendrá en los 1.109 euros que ahora marca Apple, por lo que se acaba de abrir una oportunidad increíble para renovar.
Siguen siendo casi 1.000 euros por un móvil, pero viendo cómo está afectando la crisis de la memoria a la industria, comprar ahora y ahorrarte esos 180 euros parece la mejor opción.
¿Es buen móvil el iPhone 17 después de un año de vida?
Rotundamente sí. Ya te lo contamos en nuestro análisis, y nuestra recomendación sigue en la misma línea. Apple renovó el dispositivo en 2025 con novedades interesantes: ahora tiene una pantalla a 120 Hz, una muy buena batería, un diseño compacto de mucha calidad y una cámara ideal para aquellos que no quieren dar el paso al modelo Pro.
Ahora mismo, teniendo en cuenta las subidas de precio y la oferta de Amazon, se postula como el iPhone ideal para el 95% de los usuarios. Sigue siendo el iPhone base más moderno, su renovación no llegará con grandes novedades y todo su hardware es más que suficiente para pasar los próximos años sin preocuparte de nada.
No es el móvil perfecto, pero si quieres un iPhone nuevo, este iPhone 17 debería estar en tu punto de mira. De hecho, si lo necesitas ya, cómpralo antes de que Amazon actualice el precio y empiece a basarse en el nuevo PVP de 1.109 euros que ha fijado Apple.

What is NYT Connections?
NYT Connections is one of several increasingly popular word games made by the New York Times. It challenges you to find groups of four items that share something in common, and each group has a different difficulty level: green is easy, yellow a little harder, blue often quite tough and purple usually very difficult.

It's a little more involved than something like Wordle, however, and there are plenty of opportunities for the game to trip you up with tricks. For instance, watch out for homophones and other word games that could disguise the answers.
It's playable for free via the NYT Games site on desktop or mobile.

articles.title: La Guardia Civil buscaba al mayor estafador inmobiliario de Mallorca. Lo encontraron escondido debajo del fregadero de casa de su madre
articles.text:
Nueve meses en busca y captura, y la Guardia Civil lo encontró donde empezó todo: en casa de su madre, en Calella (Barcelona), escondido en un mueble bajo el fregadero. Carlos García Roldán, 'Charly' para sus víctimas, es el cerebro de Lujo Casa, la mayor estafa inmobiliaria investigada en Baleares: 3,4 millones de euros sustraídos a al menos 235 compradores mediante viviendas que nunca existieron. La Audiencia Provincial lo condenó en diciembre a casi 15 años de cárcel. Él, simplemente, no se presentó a firmar la sentencia.
Cómo dieron con él. Los investigadores de la Guardia Civil sospechaban desde hacía semanas que García Roldán se ocultaba en la vivienda materna, mismo domicilio donde recibió la notificación de la sentencia en diciembre. Confirmarlo costó más: no salía nunca a la calle, ni a pasear ni a comprar, y dejaba que fueran sus familiares quienes hicieran los recados mientras él permanecía dentro.
Una información precisa recibida por los agentes el propio jueves precipitó por fin la orden judicial y, con autorización de entrada y registro emitida por la Audiencia balear, la Unidad Orgánica de Policía Judicial de la Guardia Civil de Baleares y Barcelona entró en la casa y lo encontró agazapado en el hueco bajo el fregadero de la cocina, entre tuberías y productos de limpieza. El juzgado de guardia de Arenys de Mar ordenó su ingreso inmediato en prisión: de vuelta a Mallorca, a cumplir la condena que esquivó durante nueve meses.
Una cronología con más giros que una novela negra
- Diciembre de 2015: García Roldán funda Promociones Lujo Casa Baleares SL, con un capital que los jueces describirían después como "meramente aparente".
- 2015-2018: La empresa anuncia más de treinta promociones sobre plano en Palma, Marratxí, Llucmajor y Algaida, aunque de esas treinta, el suelo solo se compra realmente para siete.
- Marzo de 2018: Estalla el escándalo, las denuncias empiezan a llegar a los juzgados de Palma, y García Roldán huye a Colombia.
- El 2 de septiembre de ese mismo año, con él ya prófugo, un juzgado de Palma ordena la entrada en prisión de sus dos socios, Michele Pilato y José Antonio Mir. Tiempo después, la Justicia consigue su extradición y reanuda el proceso.
- 18 de diciembre de 2025: la Audiencia Provincial de Balears lo condena a 14 años y nueve meses de cárcel por estafa agravada, pertenencia a grupo criminal, insolvencia punible y blanqueo de capitales, además de una responsabilidad civil de 457.872 euros y una multa que, de no pagarla, se convierte en 6 euros diarios de cárcel durante 45 meses más.
- Al día siguiente tiene cita y no aparece: alega que está fuera de Mallorca y que no encuentra vuelo de vuelta. La Audiencia dicta orden de busca y captura ese mismo mes. Junto a él, la Audiencia condena también a Pilato a 9 años de cárcel, y a Mir, que aportaba apariencia de solvencia técnica como supuesto constructor, a 4 años.
- Nueve meses después, el 10 de septiembre de 2026, la Guardia Civil lo localiza y lo detiene.
La primera fuga. Esta no era la primera vez que García Roldán intentaba esquivar a la Justicia. Nada más huir en 2018, buscó refugio en Buga, en el departamento colombiano del Valle del Cauca, y se instaló en casa de la abuela de su entonces pareja.
Para despistar a la orden internacional de busca y captura, adelgazó más de diez kilos y se tiñó el pelo. El disfraz funcionó una temporada, pero le delató la rutina: acudía al gimnasio y acompañaba a la abuela a hacer recados por el pueblo, hasta que esos hábitos lo situaron. Lo detuvieron en febrero de 2019 y lo extraditaron a España para que el proceso siguiera su curso.
Cómo funcionaba la estafa. Lujo Casa vendía pisos que no existían. Bajo la marca Mallorca Investment no faltaban ni folletos ni maquetas. Tenían oficinas y hasta arquitectos y constructores de verdad reforzando la ilusión de una promotora consolidada. Las fotos de las viviendas, sin embargo, salían de internet o de proyectos ajenos.
Ninguna promoción contaba con licencia de obra, aval bancario ni seguro de caución, y el dinero de los compradores jamás llegó a una cuenta especial protegida, como exige la ley. El dinero de los compradores tampoco iba a construir nada: se desviaba mediante reintegros, transferencias y endosos a sociedades como Cortecera 17 y Esparver, usadas para gastos personales.
Según los jueces, esto era “un negocio civil criminalizado", una "estructura defraudatoria diseñada, refinada y mantenida en el tiempo". Durante el juicio, García Roldán negó las acusaciones: aseguró que había avisado a los compradores de los riesgos y culpó del desastre a una "estampida" de clientes que pidieron la devolución de sus reservas a la vez. Sobre la fuga a Colombia, dijo que actuó por miedo.
Un agujero de tres millones. Los compradores, en su mayoría parejas jóvenes que buscaban su primera vivienda, entregaron entre 5.000 y más de 100.000 euros cada uno como reserva. Ahora tienen hipotecas sin casa, ansiedad por los pleitos y están sin sus ahorros. Según la sentencia, entretanto el entramado ha estado gastando el dinero captado en ropa de alta gama, coches deportivos, viajes y, sobre todo, en el juego: solo en el Casino de Mallorca, García Roldán llegó a dejarse más de 270.000 euros en cerca de 300 visitas nocturnas.
Lujo Casa es como Monica, otro caso similar: la Guardia Civil buscaba también a esta empresaria, de nacionalidad alemana, acusada de estafar con el mismo método a compradores extranjeros en la isla. El boom inmobiliario mallorquín, con extranjeros comprando sin pisar antes la isla, resulta terreno fértil para timos que se sostienen mientras nadie pregunta demasiado.

articles.title: Lenovo Legion 9i Gen 10 18" Laptop Review: A True Desktop Replacement
articles.text:
The term "desktop replacement" gets thrown around a lot when it comes to 18-inch laptops, but even the biggest and fastest notebooks usually come with compromises compared to a desktop PC.
Working and gaming on the Lenovo Legion 9i Gen 10, however, comes with almost no downsides compared to using my PC. This beast has become my favorite of all the laptops I've ever tested, but it comes at a price that's almost comical.
Lenovo aims the Legion 9i Gen 10 at both developers and gamers, which means it packs a punch. Under the hood there's a 24-core Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus, an RTX 5080 that can consume up to 175W, a massive 64GB of DDR5-4800, an ultra-high-performance SK hynix Platinum P51 2TB Gen 5 SSD, and a 99.9Wh battery.
Despite the name, laptops of this size aren't exactly suitable for laps. The Legion weighs 7.7 pounds, while the entire package comes to just over 10 pounds once you include the hefty 400W power adapter and cables. But then, devices like this aren't usually bought for their portability. It measures 15.87 x 11.69 x 1.10 inches at its thickest point, which admittedly makes it smaller than some 18-inch rivals.
The first thing that strikes you about the Legion is its looks. Like the Razer Blade, it's one of those laptops that even technophobes will compliment with a "wow." It manages to borrow cues from both gaming and professional devices, thanks to the anodized magnesium build and black aluminum lid layered with forged carbon and a lovely paint job. The laptop feels so silky and smooth to the touch that you can't help stroking it like a pet.
There's also a semi-reflective graphite camo design. It might not be to everyone's taste, but I love it. This feels more like a luxury SUV than a flashy sports car.
You do get a big "LEGION" logo that lights up on the lid, but it's off by default. There's also front ambient lighting and per-key RGB customization. The always-on light in the power button, which changes color based on the selected power profile, is nice, unless you want to play in the dark.
Build quality is magnificent: sturdy as hell, with not a hint of flex in the chassis even if you deliberately try to bend it, and a screen that won't flop around at the slightest movement. Everything just screams high-end.
Connectivity, Ports, Keyboard
Because Lenovo advertises the Legion 9i Gen 10 as a laptop for developers as well as gamers, it's not surprising to see an extensive port selection. It comes with three USB-C ports, two of which are Thunderbolt 5 with 140W power delivery, three USB-A ports, a very handy full-size SD 4.0 card reader, an HDMI 2.1 port, a headphone/mic combo port, and, something I always appreciate, a standard-size Ethernet port (Killer E3100G 2.5G).
There's also an eShutter switch on the side that instantly disables the 5-megapixel RGB+IR webcam. Wireless connectivity, meanwhile, consists of 2x2 Killer Wi-Fi 7 BE1750x and Bluetooth 5.4.
I've always found that laptop keyboards fall into the love-it-or-hate-it category.
The one on the Legion is, without a doubt, one of the best I've ever used. With 1.6mm of travel, a good level of firmness, and a slight concave dip in each key, I found typing on it to be on par with the MacBook Pro.
Another plus is the full-size numpad and arrow keys, along with a massive trackpad that's incredibly responsive. I normally hate using trackpads, but this is the only one I've felt can almost, but not quite, match a mouse when I'm working.
Display
Having loved both the OLED and Mini-LED laptops I've recently tried, I was a bit disappointed to learn that the Legion only has a glossy IPS display. Thankfully, the HDR 3840x2400 (16:10) panel is crystal clear, with excellent factory color calibration.
The inclusion of X-Rite Color Assistant, a factory color calibration utility designed specifically for select Lenovo laptops, is a godsend for anyone working with photos or videos who needs accurate color profiles. Playing the same YouTube video on my PC monitor and the Legion really highlighted the massive difference proper color calibration can make.
It might not be as jaw-dropping as OLED or as bright as Mini-LED, although 520 nits is still impressive, but this is about as good as you'll get from an IPS panel. It's certainly the best I've ever seen.
The only complaint I have is that the glossy screen is quite reflective, especially in brightly lit rooms or outdoors on a sunny day. Not that you'd want to use this thing outdoors too often.
Then there's the refresh rate. At its native resolution, the screen hits a buttery-smooth 240Hz. Drop it down to 1080p and that jumps to a blistering 440Hz.
Gaming Performance
I was expecting good things from the Legion in this department, given the powerful hardware it's packing. The LegionSpace app lets you select between Quiet, Custom, and Performance modes, and it includes an automatic GPU overclocking switch to squeeze every last drop out of this machine. There's also a custom profile for those brave enough to risk the warranty.
When plugged in (obviously) and pushed hard, the Legion's RTX 5080 reached 2,700 MHz and drew 160W while touching 74°C. That's an excellent result for a laptop GPU operating close to its 175W ceiling, leaving plenty of thermal headroom even under sustained load.
Gaming on the Legion is phenomenal. It races past the Medion Erazer Beast 18, another 18-inch laptop with a 175W RTX 5080, at the same settings and resolution. Across the six games I tried on both laptops, the Lenovo was 22% faster on average. It also destroyed the Asus Zephyrus 16, admittedly not a surprise given that laptop's 120W RTX 5080.
All titles were tested at 2560x1600. They were played without any upscaling or frame generation, and with no additional ray tracing effects enabled.
2,560 x 1,600 in Performance Mode
| Game / Scene | Settings | Avg. FPS | Min | Max | 1 % Lows | 0.1 % Lows | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Doom: The Dark Ages/ Hebeth | Nightmare | 83 | 58 | 111 | 68 | 58 | 
| Space Marine 2 / Mission 4: Servant of the Machine | High | 103 | 54 | 125 | 79 | 61 | 
| Black Myth: Wukong/ Yellow Wind Sage boss | Very High | 73 | 33 | 133 | 53 | 40 | 
| 007: First Light / Market | Ultra/High Lighting | 61 | 29 | 98 | 49 | 39 | 
| Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced / Havana | Very High | 71 | 44 | 116 | 54 | 46 | 
| Cyberpunk 2077 / Japantown driving | High settings | 104 | 63 | 128 | 73 | 47 | 
| Baldur's Gate 3 / Baldur's Gate | Ultra preset | 148 | 64 | 178 | 100 | 75 | 
| Assassin's Creed Shadows / Yamashiro | High preset | 71 | 43 | 115 | 54 | 43 | 
Synthetic Benchmarks
In 3DMark's Steel Nomad and Time Spy benchmarks, the Legion managed excellent and very good scores, respectively. Cinebench also produced above-average results for the Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus.
| Program | Test | Result | 
|---|---|---|
| 3DMark | Steel Nomad | 5,620 | 
| 3DMark | Time Spy | 21,710 | 
| Cinebench 2026 | Single Core | 572 | 
| Cinebench 2026 | Multi Core | 8,980 | 
It's not just games where the Legion excels, either. That Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus combined with a monstrous 64GB of RAM means it chews through professional workloads.
I've never found a laptop that can match my PC for editing videos in DaVinci Resolve, but the Legion's hardware, combined with that pro-level screen calibration, makes it even better for content creation than my trusty rig. It scrubs through videos without a hitch and renders them at a zippy speed.
Thermals
Keeping this much hardware under control requires a beefy cooling setup. Lenovo's Coldfront: Vapor system combines a massive vapor chamber, liquid-metal cooling, and four fans. Lenovo rates the laptop with a 300W thermal ceiling.
During a 10-minute Cinebench 2026 multicore run in Performance mode, the Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus peaked at 88°C while briefly drawing 174W. That left it 17°C below Intel's 105°C thermal ceiling, and HWiNFO recorded no thermal throttling, although the processor frequently encountered its configured power limit.
Most of the generated heat is expelled through the rear exhaust vents surrounding the power and HDMI connections. That part of the laptop becomes noticeably toasty during sustained workloads, but directing the heat backward helps keep the keyboard, touchpad, and palm rests comfortable.
Tests of the same 18IAX10 chassis measured its hottest areas at approximately 43 – 44°C, while the touchpad and palm rests remained at around 32 – 33°C.
Sound
The Legion can get very loud thanks to its six-speaker setup, consisting of four woofers and two tweeters, but audio isn't the laptop's strongest suit. The sound certainly isn't bad and, thanks to this being another device that comes with the audio-personalizing Nahimic app, you can play with the settings to get things just how you like them.
But crank the volume to maximum and you'll start to notice some shortcomings, including mild distortion in certain scenarios.
Storage
Storage performance is another highlight. The 2TB SK hynix Platinum P51 PCIe 5.0 SSD delivered sequential read and write speeds of 12,217 MB/s and 12,932 MB/s, respectively, in CrystalDiskMark.
Random 4K performance was also impressive, reaching 585 MB/s reads and 797 MB/s writes at Q32T1, while the Q1T1 test produced 84 MB/s reads and 124 MB/s writes.
The results put the P51 firmly among the fastest laptop SSDs, with its near-13 GB/s sequential write speed particularly impressive for a notebook.
Battery Life and Noise
Gaming laptops aren't famed for their battery life, especially ones this large and powerful. The Legion 9i does pack a 99.9Wh battery, putting it just under the 100Wh limit that can generally be carried on a flight without airline approval.
Longevity was pretty much what I'd expect: not great. For work, it lasted around four hours with the screen brightness at roughly 70%, running at its native resolution and with the keyboard lighting off. Testing also shows it playing more than six hours of YouTube video at 50% brightness in 720p. Don't bother with untethered gaming, for many reasons.
The Legion is on the louder side, but I've used other RTX 5080 laptops that are more offensive to the ears in terms of both volume and pitch. It hit a maximum of 57.5 decibels when pushed to the absolute limit, so don't use it in a library.
The Big Issue
So, it's an incredible laptop, but what's the big caveat? Beyond the lack of OLED and Mini-LED options, it's the price. This model normally costs a comical $5,800, though at the time of writing, Micro Center has it discounted to a still-brutal $4,500.
As we all know, the memory crisis has pushed electronics prices through the roof, as illustrated by the Steam Machine. With 64GB of RAM, the Legion was always going to carry a huge price tag, but four and a half to nearly six thousand dollars is a stunning amount of money.
It's enough to buy a full desktop with an RTX 5090 and even a monitor, though you might have to settle for just 32GB of RAM instead of 64GB.
Wrap Up
Here's the bottom line: the Legion 9i Gen 10 is the best laptop I've ever used. Not only does it tear through games and productivity programs, but it also looks and feels great. And despite being limited to IPS, the dual-mode display, with its excellent color accuracy, is beautiful. The biggest compliment I can give it is that it's the only laptop I've been happy to use instead of my desktop.
But then, for $4,500+, I'd expect nothing less. Granted, Lenovo isn't responsible for the current cost of DRAM and NAND, though that's of little consolation to buyers. Ultimately, if you have a lot of disposable income and really want a true gaming desktop replacement, very little comes close. But you might want to opt for 32GB of RAM to save around $600.
Pros
- Blistering performance in games and apps
- Gorgeous dual-mode IPS screen that reaches 440Hz
- Attractive looks
- A genuine desktop replacement
Cons
- Prohibitively priced
- OLED and Mini-LED options would have been welcome
- Noticable reflections on the glossy screen in bright rooms/outdoors
- Most people don't need 64GB of RAM

articles.title: Confira o Olhar Digital News na íntegra (11/09/2026)
articles.text:
Veja os destaques do Olhar Digital News desta sexta-feira (11/09).
Fábrica no interior de São Paulo irá produzir carros voadores
A Eve Air Mobility, subsidiária da Embraer, deu mais um passo pensando no desenvolvimento de seu veículo elétrico de decolagem e pouso vertical (eVTOL). Mas, dessa vez, o avanço não está relacionado ao carro voador em si, e sim à fábrica que será responsável por produzir as unidades em larga escala.
Sam Altman considera frear avanço da OpenAI após falhas em testes
O CEO da OpenAI, Sam Altman, disse a funcionários que a empresa considera reduzir o ritmo de desenvolvimento de inteligências artificiais avançadas. A ideia seria acompanhar o ritmo de alguns laboratórios concorrentes, mesmo que nem todas as empresas aceitem uma eventual desaceleração.
ChatGPT inventa testemunhas e depoimentos em processo judicial
A Suprema Corte do Novo México, nos EUA, aplicou uma multa a um advogado de defesa que usou o ChatGPT para elaborar um recurso de apelação criminal em um processo de assassinato. A IA inventou depoimentos de policiais e criou testemunhas fictícias.
Você provaria? IA já está criando a comida do futuro
Desenvolver um novo produto alimentício costuma exigir longos meses de testes. Mas sistemas de inteligência artificial podem otimizar essa etapa. A tecnologia não “inventa” uma receita do nada. E sim consegue identificar relações e sugerir combinações que atendam a determinados objetivos.
Alessandro Di Lorenzo é editor do Olhar Digital e formado em jornalismo pela Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS).

articles.title: La nueva película de 'X-Men' ficha a esta estrella de 'The Boys' como Ángel
articles.text:
Marvel sigue dando forma a su nueva película de X-Men. Y es que, a pesar de haber anunciado a buena parte de su reparto principal hace unas semanas, acaban de cerrar un nuevo fichaje. Concretamente, La Casa de las Ideas ya tiene al actor que interpretará a Ángel, el icónico mutante alado. El elegido es, de hecho, una estrella de la aclamada franquicia de The Boys.
Tal y como ha informad The Hollywood Reporter, el actor Asa Germann interpretará a Ángel en la nueva película reboot de X-Men. Anteriormente, su nombre ya se había vinculado a la cinta, donde sonó como uno de o¡los candidatos para el papel de Cíclope. Finalmente, aquel rol recayó en Kit Connor. Pero Marvel no quiso dejar escapar a una de las grandes estrellas jóvenes del Hollywood actual.
Así las cosas, se encargará de Ángel, un joven que se llama Warren Worthington III y que cuenta con enormes alas de plumas en su espalda. En los cómics esconde su mutación hasta que da con el Profesor X. Más adelante, el villano Apocalipsis le transforma en Arcángel, una versión malvada y oscura del personaje, con alas metálicas. Para el gran público, antes de ser Ángel en X-Men, Asa Germann es conocido principalmente por su participación en Gen V, del universo The Boys de Amazon Prime Video.
En aquella serie interpretó a Sam Riordan, un joven casi invencible gracias a su superfuerza pero que padece esquizofrenia y estrés postraumático. Sus problemas mentales son uno de los ejes principales del título, especialmente en su primera temporada. Gracias a ese papel, Asa Germann ya sabe lo que es interpretar a un personaje con superpoderes antes de Ángel en X-Men. Por lo que su fichaje parece ideal para el proyecto de Marvel. Pero no es su único papel conocido, pues también apareció en Scream 7 como Lucas Bowden. Otra gran franquicia más, por tanto, que le asienta como un nombre a seguir en la industria.
Así será la nueva película de X-Men
Tras el fichaje de Asa Germann como Ángel, el actor de Gen V se une a un reparto de lujo para la nueva película de X-Men. El elenco de este reinicio lo encabeza Sadie Sink como Jean Grey, quien ya tuvo su reciente debut en Spider-Man: Brand New Day y regresará en Avengers: Secret Wars. Junto a ella estarán Christopher Abbott como Profesor X, Adam Driver como el villano Mr. Siniestro, Kit Connors como Cíclope, Inde Navarrette como Pícara, Samara Weaving como Emma Frost y Maya Boyd como Tormenta.
Se espera que en los próximos meses se desvelen más nombres que se unan al filme. Y es que la película de X-Men será solo el comienzo de toda una Saga Mutante que durará varios años y que mantendrá vivo al UCM. Kevin Feige lo ha apostado todo a este equipo para devolver el brillo perdido al cine de superhéroes. el director Jake Schreier, quien ya dirigiera la aclamada Thunderbolts hace unos meses, se encargará de la cinta bajo un guion de Lee Sung Jin y Joanna Calo.
La nueva película de X-Men se estrena en cines el 5 de mayo de 2028.

articles.title: Microsoft’s head of comms is leaving after almost 20 years
articles.text:
Frank Shaw is leaving Microsoft after 17 years as chief communications officer. In an internal note to his team, Shaw says he’s “decided it is time for me to move on and try new things,” after supporting Microsoft’s communications for 29 years — nearly 20 years as a Microsoft employee plus time at the Waggener Edstrom agency (now We. Communications) before that.
Microsoft’s head of comms is leaving after almost 20 years
Frank Shaw has been supporting Microsoft’s communications for nearly 30 years.
Shaw has been at the heart of Microsoft’s communications since 1997, helping the company navigate multiple Windows and Office releases, CEO transitions, the all-important bet on cloud, and huge acquisitions like the $26.2 billion LinkedIn purchase in 2016 and the $69 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard in 2023.
He’s well-respected across the public relations industry, and PRWeek recently named him number one on its 2026 list of the most powerful people in the PR industry. Internally at Microsoft he’s also well-respected among executives, and has built up a reputation for being direct, but respectful. Many employees have told me over the years that they always fear an email from him for misspeaking or accidentally leaking product plans.
He’s earned a reputation outside of the company as someone who is always willing to argue with critics, correct stories, and defend Microsoft. In 2013, he ripped into Apple and the press for daring to compare iWork to Office, and he regularly appears on X to shoot down rumors or to correct information about Microsoft. At Microsoft’s 50th birthday party last year, he appeared onstage to read out a series of hilarious mean tweets about his PR activities.
I’ve been covering Microsoft for more than 25 years, and I first encountered Shaw as a naive teenager trying to get into blogging. I would post confidential Microsoft documents online at my time at Neowin, or blog about early Windows features before the company was ready to announce them. That regularly got me into trouble with Microsoft’s army of lawyers, and even got Neowin knocked offline for 24 hours.
Despite there being a great deal of mutual respect between us, I’ve upset Shaw plenty of times over the decades, leading to some heated debates or disagreements over stories. Still to this day, when Frank calls my phone, I brace myself, knowing Microsoft is either about to announce something crazy or I’ve upset the company again.
But what’s he doing next? Shaw isn’t retiring just yet, but he tells me he’s going to take a well-earned break before moving on to “other things” he wants to do. Could that be PR for an AI startup? Baking sourdough bread professionally? In a manner befitting a communications professional: He refuses to tell me.
Microsoft isn’t naming a replacement for Shaw yet, as he’s not leaving the company until the end of the year. “I’ll be here through the end of the calendar year, and the company is working through next steps, look for an update in the next few weeks,” says Shaw in a note to his team.
Here’s Shaw’s full internal memo to his communications team:
(don’t bury the lede)
After 17 years in this role and nearly 29 working with the company, I’ve decided it is time for me to move on and try new things. Takeshi and I have been talking about this for a while, and I am excited about what’s next, for me and for Microsoft. I remain optimistic about the company mission, the incredible talent on this team, and how much the company depends on us during this critical time. I’ll be here through the end of the calendar year, and the company is working through next steps, look for an update in the next few weeks. I know you will have many questions, and I’m looking forward to talking to you at our AMA here later this morning <link>
(start burying)
A while back, there was a social media trend where people answered the question, “What topic could you give a 30-minute presentation on with no preparation?” Me, I could talk about the US Marines, the changing nature of influence, sourdough starter, the Oregon Ducks, but my go to would have to be aspects of Stephen King’s the Dark Tower books, starting with “The Gunslinger;” the question then becomes which particular aspect. A quick primer, the series follows Roland Deschain, the last of the gunslingers (a mix between mayor/judge/sheriff), as he chases the man in black through time and dimensions in a quest to save the world. The question embedded throughout is if it is possible for Roland to retain his identity and meaning in a world that had moved on. The refrain is that the world moves on, move with it or fall. Can Roland move and grow, or will he be stuck? One of the concepts that sticks with me comes as we are introduced to more characters, now moving with Roland. He introduces the concept of ‘ka-tet’ to describe them. ‘Ka’ is essentially fate, or destiny, and ‘tet’ translates to a group of people, put together for a larger meaning – a group brought together with a shared mission and destiny, a group with shared goals, the willingness to sacrifice for those goals, with a deep emotional connection to each other and the ability to make and act on decisions with what can feel like supernatural speed.
I’ve always loved the evolution from the solo gun slinger we meet in book one to the team that operates throughout the later books. Roland on his own was formidable but failed in his missions, as part of a ka-tet he was in the end successful.
You, my friends, are my ka-tet. Together, we’ve accomplished amazing things. My gratefulness is endless.
We will have time together still over the next set of months as we finalize decisions and deliver great work on behalf of the company, and I will be close by after. In the Dark Tower, the traditional departure saying is “long days and pleasant nights,” and so it will be, but not until December. 😊
fxs

articles.title: HW Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing (Princeton, MIT, EPFL)
articles.text:
Researchers at Princeton University, MIT CSAIL, and EPFL published a technical paper titled “Efficient Hardware Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing.”
Abstract
“Register-Transfer Level (RTL) simulation is widely used to test hardware before it is fabricated. To allow testing for security related information flow properties, such as confidentiality and integrity, taint logic can be automatically added to the design to track how information flows through it. However, taint logic instrumented by the state-of-the-art, such as CellIFT, makes simulation-based testing prohibitively expensive: On our evaluation of Mega-BOOM (136K cells), it increases the instrumented design to 5.81x the original cell count and causes a 143.72x simulation slowdown. The taint logic could be simplified to improve simulation speed, but it will inevitably trade off its precision. This lightweight, imprecise taint logic will introduce false positives and may eventually result in even more overhead to check these false positives. This paper explores the research question of where precision is actually needed in the design to overcome the overhead of false positives. It presents CEGAR-T, a framework that automatically synthesizes taint logic that minimizes the taint-logic instrumentation overhead while guaranteeing no false positives (relative to the precise CellIFT baseline). We have implemented CEGAR-T and evaluated it on the safe instruction set problem for timing side-channel security across open-source RISC-V cores. Over all evaluated cores, CEGAR-T reduces both instrumentation and simulation overhead, in geometric-mean, from 5.64x to 1.42x and from 34.65x to 1.79x, respectively, without compromising the precision benefit of the CellIFT baseline.”
Find the technical paper here. September 2026.
Fan, Yu-Wei, Yuheng Yang, Christine Guo, SooHyuk Cho, Thomas Bourgeat, Mengjia Yan, and Sharad Malik. “Efficient Hardware Information-Flow Tracking for Pre-Silicon Security Testing.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2609.06791 (September 2026). https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2609.06791

articles.title: Lidl teste des caméras qui lisent votre plaque pour surveiller votre temps de stationnement
articles.text:
Lidl teste en Pologne l’installation de caméras destinées à la lecture automatique des plaques d’immatriculation, avec un stationnement gratuit limité à 90 minutes avant facturation. Certains parkings Lidl en France sont eux aussi équipés de caméras de lecture de plaques, mais pour réserver les places à la clientèle du magasin.
Si d’aventure vous allez passer l’été indien en Pologne, sachez que vous pouvez trouver, à l’entrée d’un parking Lidl, une caméra qui photographie votre plaque d’immatriculation, puis une seconde qui reprend un cliché à la sortie, sans ticket ni barrière. Lidl expérimente cette lecture automatisée des plaques d’immatriculation dans une dizaine de magasins polonais, à Wrocław et Poznań notamment.
En France, Lidl a déjà déployé ce type de caméras sur certains parkings, à Nice et Pierrefitte-sur-Seine, nous rapporte Le Journal du Geek, pour réserver l’accès et les places à sa clientèle. Idem pour Aldi et plusieurs centres commerciaux à Lille, Charenton-le-Pont, Vélizy-Villacoublay ou Rouen. Certains sites conservent une barrière, d’autres fonctionnent sans ticket papier. Sur l’un de ces sites, Autoplus a relevé une période gratuite de 90 minutes avant qu’un supplément ne soit facturé, sans indication de montant. Survision conçoit ces caméras avec son partenaire Scheidt & Bachmann pour les deux pays, mais leur usage est différent selon le pays.
Un test polonais à 90 minutes et un système différent en France
En Pologne, l’enseigne veut augmenter la rotation des places de stationnement et limiter leur usage par des automobilistes non clients, si bien qu’APCOA Parking Polska exploite le dispositif pour son compte et facture 150 zlotys au-delà de 90 minutes, soit environ 35 euros selon la presse locale, un montant que Lidl n’a toutefois pas confirmé. La durée déjà écoulée n’est pas remise à zéro si le conducteur ressort puis revient en moins de quinze minutes.
Chez Biedronka, concurrent polonais de Lidl, la pénalité s’élève à 200 zlotys pour un second jour de dépassement, soit environ 47 euros, mais l’UOKiK, l’autorité polonaise de la concurrence et de la protection des consommateurs, estime que la signalétique de ces dispositifs est trop peu lisible et dénonce une procédure de contestation sans interlocuteur direct.
En France, selon le RGPD, le numéro de plaque d’immatriculation est une donnée personnelle, si bien que la CNIL exige une signalétique appropriée et des durées de conservation proportionnées à la finalité du dispositif. D’ailleurs, Lidl installe des QR codes à l’entrée des parkings concernés pour informer les automobilistes de leurs droits. D’autres parkings français sont équipés de caméras de lecture de plaques, avec des tarifs très variables selon leurs gestionnaires, de 20 minutes gratuites suivies de 47,50 euros la journée complète à Parly 2, jusqu’à deux heures gratuites contre 15 euros d’achat à Mériadeck, à Bordeaux.
Certains de ces parkings sont exploités par des enseignes de la grande distribution, d'autres par des gestionnaires publics, par exemple la régie de Bordeaux Métropole.
Contentieux et risques de fraude autour de la lecture des plaques
Comme on vous en avait parlé, en France, Odile Maurin a saisi la justice au nom de l’association HANDI-SOCIAL contre des caméras de lecture de plaques, utilisées par plusieurs villes pour verbaliser le stationnement payant. L'association réclame une vérification humaine pour les véhicules de personnes handicapées, régulièrement verbalisées à tort malgré une carte mobilité inclusion visible. Ces automobilistes doivent sinon retirer un ticket gratuit à une borne ou s’inscrire au préalable dans une base de données, alors qu’ils disposent d’un droit de stationner au-delà des seules places réservées. Faute de contrôle humain à l’entrée, ce droit n’est pas vérifié sur place.
À Strasbourg, la fintech Lyf et l’opérateur Parcus font payer le stationnement à partir de la plaque reconnue à l’entrée et à la sortie, sans espèces ni carte. Contrairement à un poste de péage tenu par un employé, il n’y a donc aucune vérification humaine de la plaque affichée. Sur des forums, plusieurs automobilistes redoutent qu’un fraudeur recopie leur plaque pour faire payer un autre véhicule à leur place avec ce type de système.
Mais cela ne concerne pas les clients de Lidl en Pologne puisque l’enseigne facture seulement le dépassement au-delà de 90 minutes, sans faire de la plaque un moyen de paiement.
Mais, comme on vous le rappelait, en France, la CNIL a mis en garde sur la collecte des fichiers photographiques liés aux infractions routières.

articles.title: Carrefour brade de 350 € cette table d'arcade Pac-Man rétro à deux joueurs pour les French Days
articles.text:
Pac-Man a beau avoir fêté ses 45 ans l’année dernière, le petit glouton jaune n’a rien perdu de son attrait. Entre les bornes de collection et les mini-consoles rétro, les fabricants multiplient les objets qui font revivre l’âge d’or des salles d’arcade à la maison. La marque Arcade1Up, qui s’est fait une spécialité de ces meubles de jeu grandeur nature, arrive avec une borne originale aux couleurs de la mascotte de Namco.
Carrefour affiche la table d’arcade Head-to-Head Pac-Man à 349,99 € au lieu de 699 €, une remise de 350 € qui s’applique directement dans le panier. Le meuble est proposé en livraison à domicile, ce qui n’est pas un détail vu son gabarit.
C’est quoi, cette table d’arcade Pac-Man ?
Il s’agit d’un meuble de jeu au format table basse, dans le style des tables cocktail que l’on trouvait dans les bars et les cafés dans les années 80. Deux joueurs s’installent chacun d’un côté et s’affrontent en face-à-face, avec joysticks et boutons, autour d’un écran protégé encastré dans le plateau. L’habillage reprend les graphismes officiels de Pac-Man, avec le décor coloré caractéristique du jeu.
La table mesure environ 91 cm de long pour 58 cm de large et 74 cm de haut, et pèse une trentaine de kilos. C’est donc un vrai meuble, pas un jouet qu’on pose sur une étagère, et on est loin du design des bornes Arcade1Up plus hautes. En plus de Pac-Man, la table embarque aussi onze classiques Namco (Galaga, Dig Dug, Galaxian…). Son vrai atout reste le format table basse et l’affrontement à deux.
À ce prix, la table Pac-Man d’Arcade1Up est-elle une bonne affaire ?
Passer de 699 € à 349,99 €, c’est diviser le prix par deux. Pour un meuble de cette taille, décoré aux couleurs officielles du jeu et pensé pour durer, la remise de 350 € rend l’objet nettement plus intéressant. Le format table basse joue en sa faveur : il s’intègre dans un salon ou une salle de jeux sans le côté encombrant d’une borne verticale, tout en offrant les vraies sensations de l’époque, avec un joystick et des boutons physiques.
Quelles sont les dates des French Days ?
En 2026, les French Days de la rentrée se déroulent du 7 au 14 septembre inclus. Comme pour le Black Friday, de nouvelles promotions peuvent tomber chaque jour même si la plupart des commerçants proposent d’entrée de jeu leurs meilleures offres.

articles.title: Apple verschiebt iPhone 18 – oder streicht es komplett?
articles.text:
Apple verschiebt iPhone 18 auf Frühjahr – oder kommt es gar nicht mehr?
Neuer CEO, altes Vorgehen. In gewohnter Manier führte Apple durch die Produktvorstellung. Der neue CEO, John Ternus, trat Medienberichten zufolge kurz vor das geladene Publikum, dann hieß es mal wieder: Film ab. Längst stellt Apple neue Produkte nicht mehr live auf der Bühne, sondern in aufwendig produzierten Infotainment-Videos vor. Da kann bei der Präsentation nichts daneben gehen – weder durch technische Fehler noch durch Versprecher.
Bevor es um neue Technik ging, war sogar der ehemalige Apple-Chef Tim Cook auf der Leinwand zu sehen. Als vermeintlicher Hauptdarsteller beschrieben, reichte er den Stab nun quasi auch vor Publikum an Ternus weiter, der fortan übernahm und schnell zur Sache kam: Es ging, wenig überraschend, um iPhones. Doch anders als in den vergangenen Jahren, begann die Keynote direkt mit den neuen iPhones 18 Pro und Pro Max.
Wahrheit 1: Es gibt (noch) kein iPhone 18
Im gewohnt rasanten Tempo sprachen diverse Apple-Verantwortliche über die neuen Features der Pro-Reihe: neuer A20-Pro-Chip mit zwei „Desktop-Class“-Rechenkernen, der (natürlich) bislang schnellste iPhone-Prozessor. Neue Kamera mit variabler Blende, neue Möglichkeiten zur Videobearbeitung.
Das iPhone 18 kann davon – nichts. Denn das Gerät für „normale“ Nutzer:innen, die nicht unbedingt Kinofilme mit dem Smartphone drehen wollen, hat Apple an diesem Tag gar nicht vorgestellt. Damit bewahrheiten sich die Gerüchte zumindest schon einmal teilweise. Denn diverse Analysten und Experten hatten vorhergesagt, dass Apple den Start ins kommende Frühjahr verschiebt. Ob das stimmt – oder ob es fortan nur noch Pro-Geräte gibt –, bleibt noch abzuwarten. Letzteres wäre allerdings unwahrscheinlich.
Wahrheit 4: Apple will Whoop kontern
Im Wearable-Bereich war es offenbar Zeit für mutige Claims. Laut Apple messe kein Wearable den Herzschlag so genau wie die neuen Apple-Watch-Modelle Series 12 und Ultra 4. Eine verbesserte Sensorik und mehr LEDs sollen das ermöglichen. Mit den gesammelten Daten will das Unternehmen anderen Fitness-Wearables wie etwa dem bei Ausdauersportler:innen beliebten Whoop-Armband Konkurrenz machen. Denn die Daten nutzt das Unternehmen über diverse Apps hinweg, um daraus neue Wert zu generieren. So gibt ein Readiness-Score jetzt ähnlich wie beim Whoop Hinweise auf die eigene Leistungsbereitschaft – ganz ohne Abokosten.
Wahrheit 3: Airpods mit ANC sind plötzlich günstiger
In den vergangenen Wochen hat Apple kräftig an den Preisen geschraubt. Alte iPads und Macs kosten mehr Geld als zum Marktstart, neuere Macs sind ebenfalls nicht unbedingt günstig. Da überrascht es schon, dass Apples neue Airpods 5 jetzt immer mit Active Noise Cancelling (ANC) ausgestattet sind. Die Vorgängermodelle hatten sich hier noch in In-Ears mit und ohne Geräuschunterdrückung aufgeteilt. Die Überraschung: Mit ANC kosten die Airpods jetzt so viel wie früher ohne – 149 Euro. Es gibt auch eine teurere Ausgabe. Über die lässt sich die Lautstärke über die Stege einstellen. Kostenpunkt: 169 Euro.
Wahrheit 4: Das iPhone Duo ist richtig teuer – das Pro auch
Star der Show war aber natürlich das faltbare iPhone Duo. Wie andere aktuelle Foldables kommt es im „Reisepass“-Design. Im geschlossenen Zustand ist es in etwa so groß wie das Reisedokument. Aufgeklappt verwandelt sich das Smartphone dann schon fast in ein iPad Mini. Ein Rahmen aus Titan und spezielles Material beim Display sollen für Stabilität sorgen. Außerdem hat Apple iOS 27 auf den neuen Formfaktor angepasst. Das Dock ist jetzt auf der rechten Seite zu finden. Das soll die einhändige Bedienung erleichtern. Das Zusammenspiel aus Hard- und Software hat Apple typisch schon aus der Ferne seinen Reiz. Doch wer davon profitieren will, muss tief in die Tasche greifen. 2.299 Euro werden fällig. Mindestens.
Auch die Probleme steigen im Preis. Rief Apple im Vorjahr noch 1.299 Euro für das kleine Pro auf, sind es jetzt 1.449 Euro. Das große Pro Max kostet 1.599 Euro. Beide kommen in der Basisvariante mit 256 Gigabyte Speicher.

articles.title: Kiteworks Acquires Bonfy.AI to Fill the AI Gap in Data Governance
articles.text:
Kiteworks has announced the acquisition of AI data security company Bonfy.AI, a move aimed at extending real-time policy enforcement over sensitive data exchanged by both human users and AI agents.
Kiteworks delivers a content-sharing platform to safeguard sensitive data as it moves across enterprise networks, external organizations, and internal systems. It includes regulatory compliance, governance, and audit tracking.
Bonfy.ai is an AI‑native content‑security platform protecting sensitive data across human workflows and AI‑agent reasoning. It offers real‑time classification, contextual enforcement, and cross‑SaaS governance.
The cost of the acquisition has not been disclosed but is estimated by CTech at ‘tens of millions of dollars’.
The Bonfy technology will be used to extend Kiteworks’ policy enforcement across agent and human data exchange and usage in real time and inline across email, file sharing, SaaS applications, data repositories, Internet-facing AI assistants, and autonomous agents.
It fills, says Kiteworks, a structural gap in how enterprises protect sensitive data. Enterprises have detailed inventories of their sensitive data, but the inventories do not necessarily control what happens to that sensitive data when it is used or transferred. Bonfy technology fills this gap by classifying the data at the moment it is exchanged, and applying security policies before the transfer is completed – including when the exchange involves an AI assistant or autonomous agent.
Combining this technology with the Kiteworks control plane for secure data exchange, says Kiteworks, governs data in motion and in use through a single policy model that applies equally to people, machines, and systems across the enterprise.
“Bonfy.AI’s cutting-edge technology expands our coverage and capability to deliver the control our customers need in the AI era, and its excellent team will further accelerate the development of our unified Data Control Plane,” suggests Amit Toren, chief business officer at Kiteworks.
This is the eighth Kiteworks acquisition in five years, with each one designed to expand the firm’s data security and compliance platform.
The value of this acquisition includes a governed decision inline at runtime rather than a report after the fact; decisions based on genuine context rather than simple pattern matching; a single policy model for both human and AI workflows; enterprise-wide data exchange control; and provable compliance at the moment of decision. It becomes an extension of Kiteworks rather than a parallel product.
“Everything we build comes back to a single promise to our customers: you stay in control of your private data, everywhere it moves and everywhere it is used,” comments Tim Freestone, chief strategy officer at Kiteworks. “Inline at runtime classification is what makes that promise complete. Knowing where sensitive data lives is part of the equation, but deciding, in the instant data leaves, whether it should leave, and being able to prove that decision to a regulator months later is a big gap we’re closing.”
Bonfy was founded in early 2024 by Gidi Cohen and Danny Kibel. It emerged from stealth in June 2025 with $9.5 million in seed funding. “We built Bonfy.AI around a single idea: risk is created when data moves, not when it sits, and controlling it means reading the full context of an exchange at runtime, before it completes,” said CEO Cohen. “Kiteworks gives that technology a control plane and a reach we could not have built on our own. I’m excited to see it governing data for both people and AI agents at global scale.”

articles.title: 450 millions de dollars : la Française qui défie SpaceX bat un record
articles.text:
Paris accueille depuis mercredi quelque 120 délégations pour le premier Sommet international sur l’espace, grand-messe voulue par l’Élysée. La veille, The Exploration Company, cofondée par la Française Hélène Huby, annonçait une série C de 450 millions de dollars, la plus grosse jamais bouclée par une société spatiale européenne. Le tout à quelques heures d’un rapport de l’OCDE qui rappelle brutalement d’où repart le continent.
Le plus gros chèque du spatial européen, et une capsule à livrer
L’opération est menée par Bessemer Venture Partners, Atomico et le Scaleup Europe Fund adossé au fonds EQT. Elle porte à environ 680 millions de dollars les montants levés depuis la création de l’entreprise en 2021. The Exploration Company revendique par ailleurs plus de 2 milliards de dollars de contrats et d’engagements, une formulation qui mélange commandes fermes et intentions (aucun mot sur la valorisation, ceci dit). Ses 550 salariés développent Nyx, une capsule cargo réutilisable conçue pour ravitailler la Station spatiale internationale puis revenir sur Terre, avec un amarrage visé pour novembre 2028 et une dizaine de missions déjà réservées.
Les fonds accéléreront aussi Storm, un moteur de 180 tonnes de poussée à combustion étagée à flux intégral. C’est le choix technique du Raptor de SpaceX, réputé le plus efficace du marché et le plus difficile à maîtriser. Hélène Huby, passée par Airbus où elle pilotait le module de service européen du vaisseau Orion de la NASA, connaît bien la maison d’en face. Elle officie d’ailleurs cette semaine comme envoyée spéciale du président de la République au sommet, aux côtés de Thomas Pesquet.
Un record qui tombe dans une Europe à 0,3 %
Si vous suivez le spatial de loin, un chiffre publié mercredi par l’OCDE suffit à situer le décor : 13 satellites européens placés en orbite en 2025, soit 0,3 % du total mondial, contre plus de 4 000 pour les États-Unis et 387 pour la Chine. En 2011, le continent en pesait encore 20,7 %. Entre-temps, l’Europe a perdu les Soyouz au lendemain de l’invasion de l’Ukraine, attendu Ariane 6 quatre ans de plus que prévu et regardé les mégaconstellations américaines absorber le marché.
Lire aussi : L’Europe muscle son anti-Starlink – IRIS² grimpe à 348 satellites
La semaine en cours ressemble pourtant à un début de réplique. Le 5 septembre, l’allemand Isar Aerospace est devenu le premier lanceur privé européen à atteindre l’orbite. Au Grand Palais, Emmanuel Macron a annoncé la signature de plus de 50 contrats, pendant que SpaceX et Blue Origin déclinaient l’invitation sans fournir de motif officiel. Dans ce paysage, une levée record et une dirigeante propulsée émissaire de l’Élysée valent autant comme signal politique que comme opération financière.
