articles.title: En 2017, una niña de Virginia cavó un agujero en el patio trasero para un proyecto escolar. Nueve años después, el hueco sigue allí, pero el sitio es irreconocible
articles.text:
En 2017, el jardín de una familia del valle de Shenandoah, en Virginia, era poco más que una extensión irregular de césped donde por las noches se escuchaban grillos. Entonces Maggie, una adolescente de 14 años, decidió cavar un estanque como proyecto para su clase de agricultura. Nueve años después, aquel agujero sigue allí, pero el paisaje es completamente diferente.
Una niña, una pala y un proyecto. En otoño de 2017, Maggie investigó cómo diseñar un estanque y comenzó a excavarlo en el jardín de la casa familiar, situada en una zona rural del valle de Shenandoah. La idea nació como un trabajo para su clase de agricultura del instituto y, en aquel momento, el terreno no tenía nada especialmente llamativo desde el punto de vista natural: césped irregular y el sonido de algunos grillos.
Para la primavera de 2018 el estanque ya estaba lleno de agua y el resto de la familia se había sumado al proyecto colocando tierra, piedras y plantas alrededor de sus márgenes.
Aparecen los primeros habitantes. No tuvieron que comprar peces ni introducir anfibios para darle vida. Según recuerda Maggie, apenas unas semanas después de llenar el estanque aparecieron por su cuenta los primeros sapos americanos, atraídos por un lugar que hasta unos meses antes simplemente no existía.
Con el paso de los años se incorporaron otras especies y hoy las noches tienen un sonido muy diferente al de 2017: alrededor de Maggie's Pond pueden escucharse los trinos de las ranas arborícolas grises y las características llamadas de las ranas verdes.
El secreto. Sí, obviamente, no bastaba con construir un agujero. :ientras Maggie construía el estanque, sus padres comenzaron a investigar cómo podía utilizarse la vegetación autóctona para favorecer la biodiversidad. Alrededor del agua plantaron especies como buttonbush, Joe-Pye weed y pickerelweed, que ofrecen alimento, refugio y estructura a polinizadores y otros animales.
Posteriormente añadieron nenúfares blancos dentro del propio estanque, proporcionando lugares donde anfibios y macroinvertebrados pueden esconderse, reproducirse o protegerse de los depredadores.
De proyecto escolar a ecosistema funcional. La transformación resulta especialmente llamativa al comparar el mismo espacio en dos momentos: donde en 2017 había básicamente césped, en 2026 existe un pequeño hábitat acuático colonizado por diferentes formas de vida.
La National Wildlife Federation describe el resultado como un ecosistema plenamente funcional y el jardín terminó obteniendo su certificación Certified Wildlife Habitat, que reconoce espacios capaces de proporcionar a la fauna elementos como alimento, agua, refugio y lugares donde criar. Maggie tiene ahora 23 años y el estanque continúa evolucionando casi una década después de que terminara aquella asignatura escolar.
Alguien tuvo que dejar sitio. La historia resulta más interesante precisamente porque el estanque no fue abandonado después de recibir la nota de clase. La familia continuó plantando especies nativas, acondicionando sus márgenes y manteniendo un entorno adecuado para los animales que comenzaron a llegar espontáneamente.
Es una diferencia importante: Maggie creó el punto de partida, los animales lo encontraron por sí mismos y nueve años de vegetación y cuidados permitieron que aquel pequeño cuerpo de agua pasara de ser un proyecto escolar a convertirse en un hábitat estable.
Lo que cambia un estanque. Porque la propia familia evita presentar Maggie's Pond como una solución a problemas enormes como la pérdida mundial de hábitats o la desaparición de especies. Su enseñanza es mucho más pequeña y, precisamente por eso, tangible: proporcionar agua, vegetación nativa, refugio y lugares de reproducción puede cambiar radicalmente la cantidad de vida que encuentra acomodo en un jardín corriente.
Los sapos que llegaron pocas semanas después de llenarlo ilustran esa idea de una forma particularmente sencilla: en 2017 no podían reproducirse allí porque el estanque no existía, y un año después ya tenían un nuevo lugar donde hacerlo.
Una década de vida. Si se quiere también, Maggie's Pond tiene algo que muchos proyectos escolares no suelen conseguir: sobrevivir a la propia asignatura, a la nota correspondiente y al propio instituto. Aquella adolescente que comenzó a cavar con 14 años tiene ahora 23 y el estanque continúa atrayendo animales y proporcionando a la familia un lugar desde el que observarlos.
Nueve años después, el contraste resume toda la historia: Maggie no sabía que al abrir un agujero en un jardín prácticamente cubierto de césped estaba creando las condiciones para que la naturaleza hiciera el resto, y aquel pequeño gesto terminó convirtiendo unos pocos metros de patio trasero en una explosión de vida salvaje.

articles.title: Tiny nanolaser could cut computer energy use in half
articles.text:
Tiny nanolaser could cut computer energy use in half
A breakthrough nanolaser could let future computer chips communicate with light, potentially doubling down on speed while cutting energy use in half.
- Date:
- September 11, 2026
- Source:
- Technical University of Denmark
- Summary:
- Scientists have created an ultra-small nanolaser that could eventually allow microchips to transmit information with light instead of electricity, potentially making computers faster while cutting energy use roughly in half. Thousands of the lasers could fit on a single chip, opening possibilities for more efficient data centers, smartphones, and advanced medical sensors.
- Share:
The development of a nanolaser could mark an early step toward a future in which microchips communicate entirely with particles of light.
Researchers at DTU have created a tiny nanolaser that could eventually help make computers, smartphones, and data centers faster while using much less energy. The breakthrough was published in the scientific journalScience Advances.
In the future, thousands of these lasers could potentially be integrated onto a single microchip. Instead of moving information around a chip with electrical signals, devices could transmit data using photons, the particles that make up light.
"The nanolaser opens up the possibility of creating a new generation of components that combine high performance with minimal size. This could be in information technology, for example, where ultra-small and energy-efficient lasers can reduce energy consumption in computers, or in the development of sensors for the healthcare sector, where the nanolaser's extreme light concentration can deliver high-resolution images and ultrasensitive biosensors," says DTU professor Jesper Mørk.
Mørk co-authored the study with, among others, Drs. Meng Xiong and Yi Yu from DTU Electro.
Using Light Inside Computer Chips
Much of the internet already relies on light to carry information through fiber optic cables. Inside computers, however, data still moves through electronic circuits using electricity. That approach produces heat and can limit how quickly information can be transferred.
Nanolasers could bring optical communication directly onto microchips. By generating light signals efficiently inside the chip, they could allow information to move with very little energy loss, potentially making future devices faster, cooler, and more energy efficient.
Mørk estimates that using nanolasers in computers could reduce energy consumption by as much as half.
The compact DTU nanolaser is an important step toward that goal. Future chips designed around light-based communication would likely require thousands of extremely small, efficient lasers working together to transmit information across the chip.
Breaking the Size Limit for Lasers
The new nanolaser was created in DTU's clean room facility, DTU Nanolab. According to Mørk, the device pushes beyond the conventional limit for how small a laser can be made.
At its core is a structure known as a nanocavity, which traps and concentrates light within an exceptionally tiny space. Until now, achieving such intense confinement at this scale had been considered extremely difficult.
When researchers shine a beam of light onto the device, both photons and electrons become concentrated in the same microscopic region. This interaction allows the laser to function at room temperature while requiring unusually little energy.
The light-trapping structure used in the nanolaser was originally developed by Professor Ole Sigmund's group at DTU Construct.
Faster Devices and Lower Energy Use
The next major challenge is making the nanolaser operate using electrical power. If researchers can achieve that, the technology could have broad applications across computing, communications, and healthcare.
Computers and smartphones could potentially deliver greater performance while consuming less electricity. Data centers, which require enormous amounts of power, could also see substantial reductions in energy use, potentially leading to significant climate benefits.
In healthcare technology, the nanolaser's ability to concentrate light into an extremely small area could support ultra-sensitive sensors and high-resolution imaging systems.
Researchers estimate that the remaining technical challenges could be solved within the next 5-10 years.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Technical University of Denmark. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Meng Xiong, Yi Yu, Yury Berdnikov, Simon Klinck Borregaard, Adrian Holm Dubré, Elizaveta Semenova, Kresten Yvind, Jesper Mørk. A nanolaser with extreme dielectric confinement. Science Advances, 2025; 11 (51) DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.adx3865

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 is already an official Guinness World Record holder
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is already an official Guinness World Record holder, and it's expected to break even more records at launch — 'GTA 6’s release is a really global phenomenon in a way that few things are'
The Guinness World Records Gamer’s Edition 2027 is out now
- Grand Theft Auto 6 has already scooped up some Guinness World Records
- The Guinness World Records Gamer’s Edition 2027 recognizes a GTA 6 trailer as the most-viewed game trailer in 24 hours
- It's expected to break more records at launch, with the team keeping a "close eye" on it
The latest Guinness World Records Gamer’s Edition is here, and it shouldn't come as much surprise that the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 is already taking home records despite not having actually launched yet.
The Guinness World Records Gamer’s Edition 2027 officially lists a GTA 6 trailer as the most-viewed game trailer in 24 hours after it gained 475 million views in just one day.
As Guinness World Records Gamers Edition 2027 editor Alice Bell explains, "Grand Theft Auto 6 started breaking records before it came out. The first trailer still has the most views in 24 hours of any video game trailer, and for a while, the second trailer had the biggest video launch of anything, of all time, according to Rockstar."
"This was later beaten by Spider-Man: Brand New Day," she adds, "but 475 million views across all platforms is about 6% of the planet's population, which is incredible when you stop and think about it."
The first GTA 6 trailer arrived in December 2023, with the second dropping in May 2025 and offering a slightly longer look at the game. This was followed up by an extended look trailer with just under 27 minutes of footage last month.
The extended look first premiered on Netflix, but was later made available on YouTube.
"Netflix play their cards close to their chest, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the extended look earlier this month broke viewing records there," Bell continues.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
"I’m sure there will be player count and revenue records to check as well. And of course, we’ll be looking at things like the number of developers who worked on it (a record currently held by Red Dead Redemption 2). Needless to say, the contribution of every single developer who worked on GTA 6 is important."
She goes on to say that the team will be "keeping a close eye on launch and post-launch events" for further record-breaking achievements, adding that "GTA 6's release is a really global phenomenon in a way that few things are these days."
Rockstar Games also holds plenty of other records under its belt. Grand Theft Auto 5 is listed as both the best-selling action-adventure video game, with 225 million copies sold as of February 2026, and the most-watched game on Twitch in 2024.
The book also explores the year's biggest hardware developments, popular video game characters and franchises, major content creators, and real-life stories with achievements outside the virtual world.
It retails for $15.99 / £12.99 and is available via Amazon and in bookshops now.
Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles.

Before joining the team, he was Contributing Writer at PLAY (formerly Official PlayStation Magazine UK) and has written articles for many of the UK's other biggest gaming magazines including the likes of Edge, PC Gamer, and SFX.

Exclusivo: Galaxy S25 Plus cai de preço com cupom do Tecnoblog
Galaxy S25 Plus de 256 GB com câmera de 50 MP e chip Snapdragon Elite sai pela metade do preço no Magalu
O Galaxy S25 Plus (256 GB) está disponível por R$ 4.049,10 no Pix com o cupom TECNOBLOG250 no Magalu. Lançado por R$ 8.499, o smartphone premium da Samsung com tela AMOLED e câmera de 50 MP fica 52% mais barato e se torna uma das melhores ofertas vistas pelo Achados do TB.
O Galaxy S25 Plus possui uma tela AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,7 polegadas, entregando resolução Quad HD e taxa de quadros de 120 Hz. O painel ainda oferece brilho máximo de 2.600 nits e suporte ao recurso HDR10+.
O modelo tem uma câmera tripla traseira com sensor principal de 50 MP, capaz de gravar vídeos em até 8K e cliques com Estabilização Óptica de Imagem (OIS). A câmera frontal de 12 MP é ideal para participar de videochamadas com qualidade de imagem 4K.
Focado em alto desempenho e no Galaxy AI, o Galaxy S25 Plus adota o chip Snapdragon 8 Elite e 12 GB de RAM. Já o armazenamento interno de 256 GB pode ser um pouco limitado para quem deseja baixar muitos aplicativos, mídias e arquivos.
O smartphone topo de linha da Samsung é equipado com uma bateria de 4.900 mAh que, segundo a marca, tem autonomia de até 30 horas de reprodução de vídeo. Ele ainda tem suporte para carregamento rápido que, com um adaptador de 45 W, vai de 0 a 65% em apenas meia hora.
Na parte externa, o aparelho tem estrutura de alumínio e acabamento traseiro em vidro com Gorilla Glass Victus 2. Além disso, o certificado IP68 de resistência à água permite que ele fique submerso por até 1,5 metro por 30 minutos.
Por fim, o Galaxy S25 Plus (R$ 4.029,10 no Pix com o cupom TECNOBLOG250) oferece conexões 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, Ultra Wideband (UWB) e NFC. O modelo vem de fábrica com o Android 15, mas a Samsung fornecerá sete grandes atualizações do sistema operacional.

articles.title: Surfshark Systems Targeted by Hackers
articles.text:
VPN and cybersecurity services provider Surfshark this week disclosed a cybersecurity incident impacting certain internal data.
The incident, it says, was discovered on August 31, but initially treated as low risk. By September 2, however, the company confirmed the scope and moved to containment and remediation.
An internal test server that became accessible from the internet after being misconfigured was accessed by a threat actor, Surfshark explains in an incident report.
The server contained limited internal engineering material, including “parts of the system binaries and internal configurations for certain services,” Surfshark said.
Surfshark also identified internal, build-related credentials that had been committed to its code history and rotated them, although they did not provide access to user data or production systems serving users.
Additionally, the hackers accessed an isolated content accessibility optimization server (VPS) used as a proxy. However, no encryption keys, user identities, IP addresses, or browser traffic were exposed.
“Based on our investigation, we have confirmed that no user data and VPN services were affected,” the company said.
“The system involved was an internal engineering environment. By design, it does not store or process any user data, and it is kept separate from the production systems that deliver our service,” it added.
The company also pointed out that it does not log or retain VPN traffic and browsing activity and that no application or browser extension running on users’ devices was altered.
In response to the incident, the company contained the affected system and removed the exposure, rotated the relevant internal credentials, implemented additional security measures, and confirmed the full scope of the compromise.
“We will also execute an additional independent security audit to evaluate the security posture of the broader infrastructure environment,” Surfshark said.

articles.title: Nvidia estuda investir R$ 53 bilhões no IPO da Anthropic
articles.text:
A Nvidia está em negociações para se tornar uma das principais investidoras da oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO, na sigla em inglês) da Anthropic, que pode ser a maior da história. A fabricante de chips avalia investir até US$ 10 bilhões (cerca de R$ 53 bilhões) na operação, segundo duas pessoas familiarizadas com o assunto ouvidas pela Reuters.
A Anthropic pretende levantar até US$ 100 bilhões (cerca de R$ 530 bilhões) com a abertura de capital, em operação que poderia levar o valor da empresa para aproximadamente US$ 2 trilhões (cerca de R$ 10,6 trilhões). As negociações ainda estão em andamento e os planos podem mudar, segundo as fontes, que falaram sob condição de anonimato.
A possível participação da Nvidia não havia sido divulgada anteriormente. A entrada da empresa como investidora-âncora daria à Anthropic um importante apoio estratégico para uma oferta de proporções extraordinárias e poderia aumentar a confiança dos investidores na operação.
Investidores-âncora são instituições que se comprometem a comprar uma determinada parcela das ações antes que o IPO seja oferecido mais amplamente ao mercado. A estratégia tem se tornado mais comum em grandes ofertas, nas quais as empresas buscam levantar volumes elevados de capital.
A Anthropic não comentou as negociações. A Nvidia também não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.
Leia mais:
- Claude.AI: como usar inteligência artificial
- Ataques, espionagem, golpes e armas: Anthropic revela usos criminosos de sua IA
- NVIDIA compra gigante da IA por US$ 12,93 bilhões; entenda o que muda
Relação entre Nvidia e Anthropic se aprofunda
- Um investimento da Nvidia reforçaria uma relação que já é bastante próxima. A Anthropic depende fortemente dos processadores gráficos da empresa para fornecer a capacidade computacional necessária aos seus modelos de inteligência artificial (IA), enquanto tenta diversificar seus fornecedores de chips;
- A demanda pelo Claude, principal família de modelos da Anthropic, pressionou a capacidade computacional disponível para a empresa. Ao mesmo tempo, a startup vem buscando maior controle sobre seus custos de hardware e formou uma equipe interna para desenvolver chips personalizados para seus sistemas;
- Em novembro de 2025, a Nvidia havia anunciado que investiria até US$ 10 bilhões (cerca de R$ 53 bilhões) na Anthropic como parte de uma parceria mais ampla. Na ocasião, a Anthropic se comprometeu a comprar US$ 30 bilhões (cerca de R$ 159 bilhões) em capacidade computacional da Microsoft Azure equipada com chips da Nvidia;
- A Anthropic também tem, entre seus investidores e fornecedores de computação, algumas das maiores empresas de tecnologia do mundo, incluindo Amazon e Google;
- Em abril, a empresa afirmou que se comprometeria a investir mais de US$ 100 bilhões (cerca de R$ 530 bilhões) ao longo de uma década na Amazon Web Services (AWS), utilizando mais de um milhão de chips Trainium2 da companhia. A Anthropic também fechou acordos com Google e Broadcom para adicionar vários gigawatts de capacidade baseada em TPUs.
IPO pode elevar ainda mais o valor da Anthropic
A abertura de capital deve ser concluída antes das eleições legislativas de meio de mandato dos Estados Unidos, em novembro, segundo as fontes ouvidas pela Reuters.
Se isso acontecer, será mais um salto expressivo na avaliação da empresa. Em maio, a Anthropic levantou US$ 65 bilhões (cerca de R$ 344,5 bilhões) em uma rodada que levou sua avaliação pós-investimento a US$ 965 bilhões (cerca de R$ 5,1 trilhões).
A receita anualizada da empresa havia ultrapassado US$ 65 bilhões (cerca de R$ 344,5 bilhões) no fim de julho, contra aproximadamente US$ 9 bilhões (cerca de R$ 47,7 bilhões) no encerramento de 2025, de acordo com a própria Anthropic.
A avaliação projetada para a empresa também considera uma estimativa de receita de aproximadamente US$ 190 bilhões a US$ 200 bilhões (cerca de R$ 1,0 trilhão a R$ 1,06 trilhão) em 2028.
O possível IPO da Anthropic acontece em meio a uma sequência de grandes estreias no mercado acionário estadunidense. Até o fim de agosto, as ofertas públicas iniciais nos Estados Unidos, excluindo Empresas de Aquisição de Propósito Específico (SPACs, na sigla em inglês), haviam levantado um recorde de US$ 137 bilhões (cerca de R$ 726 bilhões), segundo dados da Dealogic.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Meta may have leaked the first look at its slim ‘Project Phoenix’ headset
articles.text:
Just a couple of weeks before Meta Connect starts on September 23rd, UploadVR posted images seemingly revealing the design for Meta’s “Project Phoenix” headset. The images, which UploadVR says were “found in the HorizonOS Prescription Lens firmware package,” suggest Meta may be looking to compete with devices like those from Xreal or Viture. These companies’ mixed reality glasses are a bit bulkier than something like Meta’s Ray-Ban AI smart glasses, but a step down from a full VR headset like Meta’s Quest 3.
Meta may have leaked the first look at its slim ‘Project Phoenix’ headset
Project Phoenix doesn’t quite look like smart glasses, but it’s much smaller than Meta’s other headsets.
This leak shows something that’s almost in between larger headsets and smart glasses, with lenses set into a slim, glasses-style frame. A shot from behind shows a wire extending from one of the earpieces, possibly for a battery or compute puck. There also appear to be outward- and downward-facing cameras in the earpieces.
Project Phoenix has been in the works for a while now, and isn’t expected to launch until next year. Google is also working on a pair of Project Aura XR glasses in a similar vein, with an external compute puck that’s wired to the frames.

articles.title: Olhar Espacial: a tempestade solar que quase causou uma guerra
articles.text:

articles.title: Where to preorder the Apple AirPods 5
articles.text:
The Apple AirPods 5 are bringing active noise cancellation to the masses, and they’re now available for preorder at a variety of retailers. They’ll officially launch on September 18th, the same day as the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, as well as the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
Where to preorder the Apple AirPods 5
The Apple AirPods 5 will hit shelves on September 18th, but you can line up your purchase ahead of time.
There are two versions this time around, just like with the last-gen model. The standard $129 model adds active noise cancelation, which was previously only found on the more expensive $179 AirPods 4 with ANC models. They’re available from Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Apple. The upgraded $149 model features a wireless charging case, longer battery life, and touch controls on the earbud stem that lets you adjust the volume without pulling out your phone. You can preorder this model at Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Apple.
We’re working on our review of the new AirPods 5. If you’re ready to buy before we’re able to post impressions, you can find more preorder links below.

articles.title: Chip Industry Week in Review
articles.text:
News from this week’s SPIE Photomask Technology + Extreme Ultraviolet Lithographyconference:
ASML and TSMC are launching an industry initiative to transition high-NA EUV lithography from current 6-inch photomasks to larger 12-inch masks, which could improve scanner productivity and eliminate some stitching constraints. The companies are targeting a 12-inch mask pilot line by 2031, with production-ready systems by 2033. TSMC plans to begin using high-NA EUV in high-volume manufacturing in 2030.
The eBeam Initiative‘s annual industry survey found 66% of semiconductor experts expect large-format photomasks to be adopted within a decade, while 94% expect mask revenue to grow this year.
imec demonstrated single-exposure high-NA EUV patterning of 22nm-pitch lines/spaces and 28nm-pitch vias using established chemically amplified resist technology, supporting layers envisioned for A14/A10 logic.
Intel Foundry and ASML said high-NA EUV has now processed more than 1 million wafers, including select production layers for Panther Lake, with Intel 18A high-NA layers meeting or exceeding comparable patterns made with conventional EUV.
Samsung formally joined the 12-inch photomask initiative and says it plans to introduce high-NA EUV into DRAM high-volume manufacturing in 2028.
D2S highlighted new PLDC techniques for improving mask uniformity and linearity, including Dynamic Maximum Dose, variable bias correction, and offline processing.
NY Creates joined the industry initiative developing 12-inch photomasks for high-NA EUV.
Arm broadens its AI push
At its Arm Everywhere conference in China, the company announced:
A next-gen edge AI platform, Arm Compute Subsystems for Mobile 2, aimed at agentic AI and cinematic mobile graphics. It features Mali G2-Ultra NX neural accelerator GPU and CPU cluster technology with scalable matrix extension 2.
A physical AI ecosystem program, Arm Total Design for Physical AI, for multiple companies across the technology stack, to boost development of robotics.
Neoverse CSS N4 for AI infrastructure with up to 128 cores per die, supporting LPDDR6, PCIe 7, and delivering up to 2X the performance, complemented by the Arm AGI CPU.
Amkor announced phase 2 of its Arizona advanced packaging and test campus, adding 60,000 square meters of cleanroom space and increasing the planned investment to approximately $12B. Construction is expected to begin in late 2027.
ASML has begun work on a new campus at Brainport Industries Campus North near Eindhoven, creating a second major site to support future manufacturing growth beyond its Veldhoven headquarters.
Memory
SK hynix outlined a strategy spanning HBM, 3D DRAM, HBF, CXL and SSDs, with memory increasingly co-designed at the system level for AI. The company identified 3D memory as a key future technology.
Kepler Computing emerged from stealth with its new high-bandwidth AI memory architecture using 3D stacking and ferroelectric materials. The company, which raised $468M, claims an order of magnitude capacity increase compared to SRAM and HBM, and expects to ramp production next year.
Global DRAM industry revenue jumped ~60% sequentially to nearly $155B in Q2. Market share leaders: Samsung 39%, SK hynix 25% and Micron 23%.
Chinese AI-chip suppliers including Huawei and Cambricon are raising accelerator prices as limited access to HBM drives up costs.
Memory research: USC-led researchers developed a vertically stackable vdW memory selector with >10¹²-cycle endurance, sub-20 ns switching and low device variability, addressing a key challenge in scaling high-density 3D memory. NUS researchers developed an on-chip pulse generator for field-free magnetic switching, cutting write energy by four orders of magnitude and pointing to faster, lower-power magnetic memory.
Analog Devicesagreed to acquireAlif Semiconductor in an all-cash transaction for $1.35B, for its high-efficiency AI-native MCUs and fusion processors optimized for on-device, physical AI.
OpenAI is working with Samsung on next-gen chips, with OpenAI Korea chief Harrison Kim saying the companies have made significant progress in joint production and research, reports Reuters.
Raking it in
Ayar Labs raised $150M and announced Wiwynn made a strategic investment earlier this year for its continued transition to high-volume manufacturing of CPO for AI scale-up.
Xanadu and ASML will collaborate on advanced lithography for photonic quantum chips to improve patterning and reduce optical loss.
The U.S. Department of Commerce finalized $775M in previously announced CHIPS R&D awards for domestic quantum semiconductor development and manufacturing, including $375M for GlobalFoundries and $100M each for Rigetti, D-Wave, PsiQuantum, and Quantinuum.
Market data
Revenue for the world’s top 10 foundries rose more than 11% sequentially to a record ~$53B in Q2, according to TrendForce.
The data-center semiconductor market will reach $1.5T by 2031 as AI drives increasing demand for logic, memory, optical interconnects and power devices, predicts Yole Group. Advanced packaging and HBM capacity are emerging as major bottlenecks, while AI rack power could approach 1 MW by the end of the decade.
Financials
TSMC (August revenue up 53% YoY) and IQE (1st half up 40% YoY).
The U.K. government released an expanded study of the country’s semiconductor sector, identifying 703 companies and estimating that dedicated semiconductor businesses generated £10.6B in revenue in 2025.
SEMI Europe published a position paper outlining nine recommendations for the EU Chips Act 2.0, including broader First-of-a-Kind eligibility, six-month permitting timelines, and measures addressing energy, infrastructure, and manufacturing costs. It also called for balanced funding, so leading-edge projects don’t crowd out pilot lines, mature and specialty technologies, and advanced packaging.
Keysight entered an agreement to support the EU’s Chips JU initiative by making its EDA software and training available to semiconductor startups and small and medium-sized enterprises.
TU Eindhoven and European collaborators fabricated edge AI processors that combine RISC-V processors with specialized AI accelerators and memory-centric and neuromorphic computing.
Americas
Silicon Labs opened a new R&D lab at its Austin headquarters aimed at advanced chip design and testing.
Companies are exploring Argentina‘s remote, cold Patagonia region for data center buildout, per Reuters.
Qolab and SkyWater signed a multi-year foundry agreement to manufacture superconducting quantum devices using SkyWater’s new SC250 platform.
Samsung Electronics and Mistral AI formed a strategic partnership to deploy customized, on-premises AI models across Samsung’s semiconductor operations for defect detection, equipment optimization, and yield improvement. Samsung also led Mistral AI’s Series D funding round and took a strategic equity stake.
Fundings, IPO
Altera is reportedly preparing an IPO that could raise more than $2B. Silver Lake owns 51% of Altera, while Intel retains 49%.
NLM Photonicsexpanded funding to commercialize organic photonics, including an investment from Mitsubishi Chemical.
States That Gave Data Centers Billions in Tax Breaks Are Now Ripping Up the Deals (WSJ)
New Technologies
PDF Solutions debuted Exensio Aurora, its new scalable analytics architecture. The product is designed to handle semiconductor manufacturing data at petabyte scale and securely deploy agentic AI across manufacturing operations and the supply chain.
Taiyo Holdings and imec demonstrated a 3-layer RDL with 700nm wiring and vias on 300mm wafers using Taiyo’s new photosensitive dielectric material. The work advances fine-pitch RDL technology for advanced packaging.
Infineon introduced the TDA235E5 and TDA235E0, a dual-phase smart power stage family designed to meet growing power density requirements of next-generation AI accelerators and vertical power delivery modules. The new offerings will deliver benchmark power density exceeding 2 A/mm².
imec has moved its 96-band hyperspectral linescan sensor into commercial availability for camera and satellite developers. The CMOS-based sensor has a spectral range of 450 to 900nm, improves signal-to-noise ratio by 40% over its predecessor, and integrates its spectral filters directly on-chip.
CoreWeave launched “Physical AI Field Engineering” this week, a new offering built to help manufacturers integrate physical AI into their engineering processes.
Smartphone chips
Apple unveiled new products under new CEO, John Ternus, including its 2nm A20 Pro chip for the iPhone 18 with 50% more memory bandwidth and integrated neural accelerators, as well as the company’s first foldable phone, iPhone Duo.
Powering its new Mate XT 2 trifold smartphone, Huawei launched the first commercial application of its Kirin 9050 Pro chip with LogicFolding architecture, with 42% better performance than its predecessor, per SCMP. (Read a related technical paper: Huawei’s Tao Chip Was Supposed to Melt?)
Connecting data centers
OIF published the implementation agreement for 1600ZR Coherent Interfaces, doubling the capacity of its 800ZR specification.
Meta and Panmnesia proposed an architecture that lets an entire data center operate as one chip by placing CPUs, accelerators, and memory in a single CXL-over-optics-based domain, with a high-fan-out non-blocking switch, a link acceleration unit and a fabric controller to bound latency variability.
Adoptions and certifications
Cadencequalified its EDA tool flow to run natively on AWS Graviton, including front-end design and verification, synthesis, place-and-route, and timing sign-off. Annapurna Labs is now designing future-gen Graviton CPUs using the Cadence flow.
Japan’s NanoBridge Semiconductor adopted Siemens EDA’s FPGA tools for its low-power, harsh-environment FPGAs for aerospace, automotive, and critical infrastructure.
d-Matrix will use NVIDIA’sNVLink Fusion to connect its upcoming Raptor inference processors directly into NVIDIA-based data center systems. Raptor is expected to complete final design this year, with compatible rack-scale systems targeted for 2027.
Redington will distribute Siemens EDA’s Xcelerator portfolio of industrial software across Africa.
Research
Kyocera and Tohoku University developed an isolator-integrated photonics chip that reduces back-reflected light by about 95%, enabling faster, energy-efficient AI data centers.
CEA-Leti, Spintec, and Université Paris-Saclay researchers demonstrated a hybrid nanoelectronic Ising machine — combining hafnium-oxide ReRAM devices with stochastic MTJs — with an intrinsic annealing mechanism that could pave the way for more compact, faster, and energy-efficient hardware accelerators.
Harvard researchers co-designed a layered semiconductor and a metasurface, so every part of the device, including electronic states, optical fields, and geometry, works together toward efficient frequency conversion at a given wavelength, which could help miniaturize photonics and quantum technologies.
Researchers in Japan have demonstrated the first epitaxial growth of single-crystalline polar wurtzite NbAlN on GaN. An optimized NbAlN/GaN heterostructure more than tripled sheet electron density while retaining high room-temperature mobility, suggesting a potential new route to higher-performance GaN power and RF devices.
Security
AI threats
Google published new warnings on agentic AI-enabled cyberthreats this week, sounding alarms for expanded SW supply chain risks, threats to AI IP, and increased LLMjacking efforts.
Independent researchers found that a swarm of OpenAI agents reportedly hacked a German wiki site to create a message board earlier this year, in an incident that appears to have preceded the similar Hugging Face breach in July.
Anthropic published an updated cybersecurity advisory after discovering a fourth instance of a Claude model gaining unauthorized access to a third-party system.
AWS released Deception Benchmark, a new framework designed to test whether AI models can “distinguish real vulnerabilities from code that looks risky but is actually safe.”
A new IAPS report on AI data center security called for new industry security standards, increased cross-company incident intelligence sharing, and security-focused supply chain realignment in the face of emerging AI threats to data centers.
The FBI published its first-ever cyber strategy roadmap, with the document outlining a shift toward more proactive cybercrime disruption efforts.
Cisco updated its Secure Firewall Management Center advisory to confirm active exploitation of a critical authentication-bypass vulnerability that can let unauthenticated remote attackers gain root access.
CERT Polska warned that attackers are actively exploiting a chain of six MikroTik RouterOS vulnerabilities. Two flaws can be combined to take full control of exposed routers through SSH without authentication.
The NSA, FBI, and CISA issued a joint advisory covering cybersecurity threats tied to Chinese AI companies conducting industrial-scale distillation campaigns against US frontier AI models. Chinese companies have “likely extracted billions of tokens across millions of exchanges/requests from U.S. frontier AI models” since 2024, the agencies said.
SK keyfoundry and automotive mixed-signal semiconductor supplier Elmos announced a new long-term wafer supply deal alongside plans to expand the companies’130nm technology collaboration.
Microchip announced a strategic collaboration with Longhorn Automotive to integrate its VS700 ASA-ML chipsets into camera systems for ADAS and in-cabin sensing.
Cadence’s Amol Borkar examines how this technology will improve even further in the future, why the focus isn’t just about faster processors, and why this is so important for edge systems.
Quantum
SkyWater launched SkyWater Quantum Solutions, combining superconducting, quantum photonics, heterogeneous integration, and advanced packaging capabilities to help move quantum technologies into manufacturing.
Fujitsu developed a working prototype of a diamond-spin quantum computer that incorporates tin-vacancy (SnV) centers into photonic ICs, an important step toward a modular architecture.
LUMI AI Factory selected IQM’s staged path to deploy the EU’s first superconducting quantum computer with logical qubits, at IT Center for Science in Finland, as part of a hybrid HPC, AI, and quantum computing platform.
Quantum research
A University of Chicago researcher found that a quantum computer could “use high-powered lasers as ‘optical tweezers’ to capture and control individual atoms of helium,” offering faster tunneling, faster transport, and controllable motional qubits, compared to designs based on lithium.
An MIT researcher tested GPT-5.6 Sol’s ability to run measurements on an uncalibrated six-qubit chip and found that, when the signals were clear, Codex completed a standard sequence of measurements with little researcher intervention.
Workforce, Education
The National Network for Microelectronics Education formed its first Industry Advisory Committee, bringing together leaders from Lam Research, Intel and others to guide U.S. semiconductor workforce strategy. The group will help align education and training programs with industry needs as the sector faces a projected shortfall of 127,000 to 157,000 workers by 2030.
India is providing EDA tools to 13 engineering colleges under its chips to startup (C2S) program.
The U.S. State Department formally launched Foundry School, a training program for engineers, technicians and industry leaders, with instruction spanning semiconductors, factory design, automation, supply chains and manufacturing operations.
Reducing variation in manufacturing, monitoring behavior over time, and targeting specific workloads can have a big impact on power, performance, and area/cost.

articles.title: JBL's new Cove speakers can be linked to form a whole-home audio system - Tech Guide
articles.text:
JBL has launched a new range of speakers called JBL Cove which can be combined to form a whole-home Wi-Fi audio system to produce a high-quality multi-room listening experience.
There are three wireless speakers in the range that can operate on their own as stereo pairs or as part of a connected home audio system, which can be controlled through the JBL One app.
JBL Cove brings the iconic JBL room-filling sound, along with Dolby Atmos support on some models and flexible listening room by room without the need to regroup or reset the speakers.
It’s really easy to transform your space and create an immersive listening experience with the new JBL Cove series.
Included in the series are:
– JBL Cove M1 ($299) – compact design for effortless everyday listening
– JBL Cove P1 ($599) – portable with battery-powered convenience and immersive Dolby Atmos sound
– JBL Cove X1 ($649) – flagship performance featuring four tweeters and dual woofers for powerful room-filling audio with Dolby Atmos
Users can place the speakers in any room and JBL will do the rest.
The proprietary Constant Sound Field can be used to allow the speakers to self-tune to your room while AI Sound Boost can optimise performance based on where they are placed and how you listen.
“Consumers across the world are increasingly seeking audio solutions that seamlessly fit into their daily lives and living spaces – with straightforward set-up, clean aesthetics and value for performance as key deciding factors,” said Grace Koh, General Manager and Vice President, Consumer Audio, HARMAN Asia Pacific.
“With JBL Cove, we’re setting a new benchmark for the future of JBL home audio, combining JBL Legendary Sound, ease of use and flexible performance in a system designed for modern homes.
“Whether enjoying a quiet cup of coffee or hosting friends for an intimate gathering, consumers can effortlessly fill their spaces with exceptional sound that amplifies ambience. This launch marks an important step in our vision to help more people across the region experience immersive, high-quality audio in the place that matters most: the home.”
To set up a home system with JBL Cove, customers just need to create a group on the JBL One app.
And from here it’s easy to control the speaker you want to listen to, whether you want to group them together or play them individually.
The Cove speakers also work with JBL Bar Series MK2 soundbars, which makes it easy to expand from music listening to creating an immersive home theatre experience.
Users can add the JBL Cove speakers as rear channels through the JBL One app to create a Dolby Atmos home theatre setup.
And you can take your music, playlist or TV audio with you.
Just press and hold the Moment button and your audio moves with you without needing to get out your phone or open the app.
Pricing and availability
JBL Cove speakers will be available in black at Harvey Norman, JB Hi-Fi, The Good Guys, Bing Lee, amazon.com.au and JBL.com.au from 1st of October 2026,
JBL Cove M1 is priced at $299.00, JBL Cove P1 is $599.00, and JBL Cove X1 costs $649.00.

articles.title: Les bénéfices de Jaguar Land Rover s’effondrent, 4 000 licenciements prévus
articles.text:
Jaguar, qui a longuement été au bord de l’extinction, pourra-t-il être sauvé par Land Rover ? Vu la situation assez catastrophique du groupe, il y a de quoi douter. Le contexte est tel que le géant a confirmé à ses employés la mise en place d’un programme de départs volontaires. Jusqu’à 4 000 postes pourraient ainsi être supprimés sur les deux prochaines années. S’il est moins spectaculaire que chez Volkswagen, ce nettoyage demeure révélateur.
L’objectif principal pour assurer la survie du groupe est d’économiser près de 2 milliards d’euros d’ici 2028. La réduction des dépenses est une chose, certes, mais elle n’a réellement de sens que si des bénéfices existent. Or, ces derniers sont devenus absolument catastrophiques. Sur le dernier exercice fiscal, les bénéfices avant impôt de Jaguar Land Rover sont ainsi passés de 2,9 milliards à seulement 16 millions d’euros en l’espace d’un an.
Cyberattaque, douanes et concurrence : un concours de circonstances fatal
Cela représente une baisse monumentale de 99 % liée à de multiples facteurs étant tous tombés au pire moment. L’importante cyberattaque de 2025 a bloqué pendant plusieurs semaines les chaînes de production du groupe alors que les droits de douane du gouvernement Trump ont fortement impacté les ventes aux États-Unis. En parallèle, il a fallu composer avec la concurrence chinoise, qui a chipé de grosses parts de marché.
Land Rover a donc pris très cher, contrairement à Jaguar, qui a été bien épargné… Logique, il n’y a plus aucun modèle au catalogue, ce qui est finalement pire ! En attendant la Type 01 qui risque de faire des vagues, le félin est pour le moment complètement engourdi en n’ayant rien à proposer. Concernant le plan de départs volontaires, les dernières sources précisent que ce sont les postes de direction et de recherche et développement qui sont concernés.
Pas de soutien financier du gouvernement britannique
Les ouvriers chargés de la production seraient donc épargnés. Mais cela n’a pas encore été officiellement confirmé. On ignore d’ailleurs si les 4 000 départs seront bien tous volontaires. Des licenciements forcés ne seraient pas à exclure si la situation venait encore à se dégrader. Cela est d’autant plus inquiétant que le gouvernement britannique exclut pour l’instant toute aide au groupe automobile.
Dans une interview accordée à la BBC, Jonathan Reynolds, le secrétaire d’État britannique aux Entreprises, explique en effet qu’ « une entreprise de la taille de Jaguar Land Rover, qui est une immense réussite britannique, voit le nombre de personnes qu’elle emploie directement varier à différents moments de son cycle d’activité ». Aucun soutien ne sera donc prévu, même si un « investissement à long terme dans l’avenir de l’entreprise » n’est pas hors de propos.

KI-Bewerbungsgespräche: Wenn der HR-Chatbot auf Waschbären-Protokolle hereinfällt
Ein satirisches Video des Influencers Graham Zip demonstriert aktuell die Schwächen von automatisierten Bewerbungsgesprächen. In einem auch auf YouTube veröffentlichten Clip antwortet der Satiriker auf die Fragen des KI-Avatars Dana Whitfield mit einer reinen Aneinanderreihung sinnfreier Begriffe.
Statt den Bewerber auf seine unlogischen Antworten hinzuweisen, greift das Sprachmodell den Unsinn auf und integriert ihn nahtlos in das weitere Gespräch. So zeigt sich die Maschine etwa angetan von der angeblichen Erfahrung des Bewerbers mit „Waschbären-Protokollen“ und zwei Mullverbänden.
Schwächen von Sprachmodellen im Recruiting
Dieses Verhalten beleuchtet ein technisches Problem aktueller Sprachmodelle, die konzeptionell auf Konversation und Zustimmung trainiert sind. Wenn Nutzer:innen den vorgegebenen inhaltlichen Rahmen verlassen, versuchen die Modelle weiterhin, den Dialog fortzusetzen, anstatt sachliche Fehler zu korrigieren.
Laut Futurism offenbart dieser Vorfall die mangelnde analytische Tiefe der eingesetzten Personal-Werkzeuge. Die Systeme überprüften die inhaltliche Plausibilität der Aussagen offensichtlich nicht, sondern berechneten lediglich die wahrscheinlichste sprachliche Antwort auf die Eingabe.
Automatisierte Filter für Personalabteilungen
Der zunehmende Einsatz solcher virtueller Recruiter resultiert in der Praxis oft aus einer schlichten Überlastung der entsprechenden Fachabteilungen. Die Unternehmen erhalten eine wachsende Flut an Bewerbungen, die ihrerseits häufig von Textgeneratoren geschrieben wurden.
Um diese Mengen zu bewältigen, setzen die Firmen auf automatisierte Video-Interviews als ersten Filter im Auswahlprozess. Die Software soll geeignete Kandidat:innen vorqualifizieren, bevor ein Mensch den weiteren Prozess übernimmt.
Die Leichtigkeit, mit der sich der KI-Avatar im Fall von Graham Zip manipulieren ließ, stellt den Nutzen dieser Vorauswahl grundsätzlich infrage. Wenn ein System nicht zwischen relevanten beruflichen Qualifikationen und völligem Nonsens unterscheiden kann, liefert es dem einstellenden Unternehmen keine belastbaren Daten.
Die Automatisierung des ersten Kontakts mag auf dem Papier zwar Zeit sparen, birgt in der Praxis jedoch das Risiko, qualifizierte Fachkräfte durch fehleranfällige Prozesse abzuschrecken. Gleichzeitig zeigt der aktuelle Fall, dass die derzeitige Generation der Personal-Bots noch weit davon entfernt ist, ein menschliches Urteilsvermögen zu ersetzen.
Lustig anzuhören, aber aus der Vorauswahl für den Job wäre er sicher rausgeflogen. Die Lady kam mir übrigens bekannt vor, die will auf Youtube ständig mitten in irgendwelchen Clips plötzlich mein Haus kaufen.

articles.title: Scientists just made quantum computer operations 1,000 times faster
articles.text:
Scientists just made quantum computer operations 1,000 times faster
A new quantum computing method can make advanced operations more than 1,000 times faster, potentially removing a major barrier to reliable quantum machines.
- Date:
- September 11, 2026
- Source:
- Chalmers University of Technology
- Summary:
- Researchers have found a way to perform certain quantum operations more than 1,000 times faster, cutting thousands of repeated control cycles down to just one. The advance could reduce errors and bring reliable, fault-tolerant quantum computers closer to reality.
- Share:
Quantum computers remain highly vulnerable to errors and tiny disturbances from their surroundings. The longer a quantum operation takes to complete, the more time there is for those errors to build up. Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden have now developed a method that can perform a broad range of advanced quantum operations more than a thousand times faster. The advance tackles a major obstacle in the field and could help move quantum computing closer to becoming fault-tolerant.
Quantum computers could eventually transform areas such as drug discovery, energy technology, cryptography, artificial intelligence, and logistics. Before that can happen, however, these machines need to become much more dependable.
Why Quantum Computers Are So Error-Prone
A major challenge is that quantum computations can be disrupted by extremely small environmental effects. Electrical noise, cosmic radiation, and overheating can all introduce errors while information is being processed.
Traditional computers can experience errors too, but decades of development have produced reliable error correction methods that can quickly detect and repair them. Quantum systems are much harder to protect because the information they use is extraordinarily delicate.
"The fundamental building blocks of quantum computers, known as qubits, are so sensitive that even the smallest disturbance can cause the quantum state to deviate from the target, resulting in the loss of information. If too many errors accumulate before they can be corrected, the computation can fail," says Lei Du, researcher in Applied Quantum Physics at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden, and lead author of the theoretical study published in the journal Physical Review Letters.
A Different Way to Protect Quantum Information
To make quantum computing more resilient and eventually fault-tolerant, researchers are investigating new ways to shield quantum information from errors. One promising strategy uses so-called bosonic quantum codes*.
Instead of assigning quantum information to individual qubits, this approach stores it in microwave fields inside superconducting circuits.
"Rather than storing quantum information in individual qubits, bosonic codes encode information in the microwave fields found within superconducting circuits. This approach has been shown to provide stronger protection against certain types of errors," explains Tangyou Huang, researcher in Quantum Technology at Chalmers and co-author of the study.
Quantum Operations More Than 1,000 Times Faster
Working with bosonic quantum codes is not simple. Creating and controlling the required quantum states has traditionally involved guiding a quantum system through thousands of repeated driving cycles.
That process can take considerable time, and every additional cycle creates another opportunity for outside disturbances to interfere with the calculation. In quantum computing, speed is therefore closely tied to reliability.
Chalmers researchers Lei Du and Tangyou Huang have now proposed a different strategy. Rather than constructing the desired quantum states one small piece at a time, their method can perform a wide variety of operations much faster.
"Our method shows that a diverse range of quantum operations on bosonic states can be completed within a single driving cycle, rather than the several thousand cycles that have been required previously. This makes the operations both faster and more efficient, while reducing the risk that disturbances will corrupt the information before the process is finished. It represents an important step towards fault-tolerant quantum computers," says Lei Du.
Quantum Lattice Gates Provide a Shortcut
The new approach is built around Quantum lattice gates, a recently proposed universal set of quantum gates developed by the same research team.
These gates act somewhat like shortcuts. Instead of requiring a long sequence of repeated control steps, they can allow the intended quantum operation to be completed in just one driving cycle. That could make the process faster, simpler, and less vulnerable to errors.
"You can think of it like building a large Lego castle. Instead of assembling it brick by brick and risking mistakes along the way, quantum lattice gates act like pre-built Lego modules that can be connected quickly and efficiently," says Tangyou Huang.
Designed for Superconducting Quantum Computers
The technique is especially well suited to superconducting quantum computers, which are among the most prominent technologies being developed in the international push toward large-scale quantum computing.
Chalmers University of Technology is also using superconducting technology as it develops a 100-qubit quantum computer.
"A key advantage of our approach is that it can be implemented using existing superconducting quantum circuit platforms. We are already discussing possible experimental realizations with colleagues at Chalmers, and we hope to see a demonstration of the method in the near future," says Tangyou Huang.
The researchers say the work addresses a central problem facing the field: efficiently producing and controlling quantum states that are capable of helping correct errors.
"Our results address one of the major bottlenecks in the field: how to quickly and reliably create and control the error-correcting quantum states that could play an important role in future quantum computers," says Lei Du.
More About Bosonic Codes, Quantum Lattice Gates and Floquet Control
*Bosonic quantum codes store quantum information in the states of, for example, microwave or optical resonators rather than in individual qubits. They are considered a promising tool for quantum error correction because they can provide built-in protection against certain types of errors.
Quantum operations are needed to process that stored information. Quantum lattice gates are a recently proposed collection of basic building blocks that can be used to control bosonic quantum states. By combining and designing these gates, researchers can carry out a wide range of more complicated quantum operations.
One method for implementing these operations is known as Floquet control, which uses periodic control signals to drive a quantum system. Earlier Floquet-based techniques have generally depended on slower processes involving many repeated driving cycles. The approach developed at Chalmers can instead perform quantum lattice gates directly in a single driving cycle, making some operations more than a thousand times faster.
More About the Research
The scientific paper "Single-Period Floquet Control of Bosonic Codes with Quantum Lattice Gates" has been published in Physical Review Letters. The authors are Tangyou Huang, Lei Du, and Lingzhen Guo. The researchers are affiliated with Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden and Tianjin University in China.
The research was funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (NSFC), the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology (WACQT), and the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Chalmers University of Technology. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Tangyou Huang, Lei Du, Lingzhen Guo. Single-Period Floquet Control of Bosonic Codes with Quantum Lattice Gates. Physical Review Letters, 2026; 137 (6) DOI: 10.1103/tnb8-3m8m
